While the chloroplast genome provides invaluable phylogenetic information, it represents only a fraction of the total genetic variation. Future research should integrate this data with nuclear genomic markers, such as those from the highly polymorphic microsatellite loci or single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), to gain a more comprehensive understanding of the genetic architecture and diversity of Muscat Hamburg. Furthermore, comparative analyses with a broader range of *Vitis* germplasm could identify unique chloroplast haplotypes that may be linked to specific traits, such as aroma profiles or disease resistance.

Conclusion

In conclusion, we have successfully assembled and characterized the complete chloroplast genome of *Vitis vinifera* Muscat Hamburg. The genome exhibits the typical quadripartite structure and encodes 133 genes, consistent with other grapevine cultivars. The identification of 54 cpSSRs provides a new set of markers for genetic studies. Phylogenetic analysis firmly establishes the maternal lineage of Muscat Hamburg within the *V. vinifera* clade. This high-quality chloroplast genome sequence will serve as a fundamental resource for molecular breeding, cultivar authentication, and evolutionary biology studies of *Vitis* species, contributing to the sustainable development of the global grape and wine industry.

References

Doyle, J. J., & Doyle, J. L. (1987). A rapid DNA isolation procedure for small quantities of fresh leaf tissue. *Phytochemical Bulletin*, 19, 11-15.

Jansen, R. K., Kaittanis, C., Saski, C., Lee, S. B., Tomkins, H., Alverson, A. J., & Daniell, H. (2006). Phylogenetic analyses of *Vitis* (Vitaceae) based on complete chloroplast genome sequences: effects of taxon sampling and phylogenetic methods on resolving relationships among rosids. *BMC Evolutionary Biology*, 6(1), 32.

This, P., Lacombe, T., & Thomas, M. R. (2006). Historical origins and genetic diversity of wine grapes. *Trends in Genetics*, 22(9), 511-519.

Wicke, S., Schneeweiss, G. M., dePamphilis, C. W., Müller, K. F., & Quandt, D. (2011). The evolution of the plastid chromosome in land plants: gene content, gene order, gene function. *Plant Molecular Biology*, 76(3-5), 273-297.

title: The cardiovascular protective effect and mechanism of calycosin and its derivatives
text: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) remain the leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, underscoring the urgent need for effective preventive and therapeutic strategies. Calycosin, a representative isoflavonoid isolated from Astragalus membranaceus, has attracted increasing attention for its diverse pharmacological properties, particularly its cardiovascular protective effects. Both in vitro and in vivo studies have demonstrated that calycosin alleviates endothelial dysfunction, inhibits vascular smooth muscle cell proliferation and migration, suppresses oxidative stress and inflammation, and attenuates myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury and cardiac hypertrophy. These effects are mediated through multiple signaling pathways, including the PI3K/Akt/eNOS, MAPK, NF-κB, Nrf2/HO-1, and AMPK pathways, as well as modulation of estrogen receptor signaling and gut microbiota-derived metabolites. Notably, emerging evidence indicates that structural modification of calycosin yields derivatives with improved bioavailability, metabolic stability, and enhanced cardioprotective potency. For instance, calycosin-7-O-β-D-glucoside and various esterified or glycosylated analogs exhibit superior antioxidant and anti-apoptotic activities in cardiomyocytes and endothelial cells. Furthermore, calycosin and its derivatives regulate autophagy, mitochondrial function, and epigenetic modifications, contributing to their multifaceted cardiovascular benefits. Despite these promising findings, most studies remain preclinical, and issues such as poor water solubility, limited oral absorption, and insufficient clinical validation hinder their translational application. This review summarizes the current understanding of the cardiovascular protective effects of calycosin and its derivatives, highlights the underlying molecular mechanisms, and discusses future research directions, including structure-activity relationship optimization, nanocarrier-based delivery systems, and well-designed clinical trials. Collectively, calycosin and its derivatives represent promising candidates for the prevention and treatment of CVDs, warranting further investigation.

title: Organization model, vertical integration, and farmers' income growth: Empirical evidence from large-scale farmers in Lin'an, China
text:
Organization model, vertical integration, and farmers' income growth: Empirical evidence from large-scale farmers in Lin'an, China

Abstract

Using survey data from 326 large-scale farmers in Lin'an District, Hangzhou, China, this study examines how different organization models and degrees of vertical integration affect farmers' income growth. Three dominant models are compared: cooperative-led, enterprise-led, and self-organized family farms. An ordinary least squares regression and a propensity score matching approach are employed to address selection bias. Results show that vertical integration significantly raises household agricultural income, with enterprise-led models producing the strongest effect, followed by cooperative-led models, while purely self-organized farms lag behind. The income advantage operates mainly through input cost reduction, price premium capture, and reduced market transaction uncertainty. The findings suggest that fostering deeper vertical linkages, rather than merely scaling up farm size, is central to sustained income growth for large-scale farmers.

Keywords: vertical integration; organization model; farmers' income; large-scale farmers; Lin'an

1. Introduction

Raising farmers' income remains a central objective of agricultural policy in China. Since the 2010s, farmland transfer has accelerated in the Yangtze River Delta, giving rise to a stratum of large-scale farmers who cultivate far more land than the average household. Yet scale alone does not guarantee prosperity. Many large-scale operators face volatile input prices, weak bargaining power, and thin margins, prompting interest in how they organize production and market exchange.

Vertical integration, understood here as the coordination of production, processing, and marketing stages within a single governance structure or through contractual linkage, is widely viewed as a mechanism for capturing downstream value and stabilizing returns. Lin'an, a mountainous district in western Hangzhou known for bamboo shoots, hickory nuts, and tea, offers a useful setting: it hosts a dense network of cooperatives and agribusiness enterprises alongside independent family farms, creating natural variation in organization models.

This paper asks two questions. First, does vertical integration raise the agricultural income of large-scale farmers? Second, do different organization models generate different income effects? The contribution is threefold: it distinguishes organization models rather than treating integration as a binary, it applies matching methods to reduce selection bias, and it provides micro-level evidence from a relatively understudied peri-urban mountain economy.

2. Materials and Methods

2.1 Study area and data

Data were collected in Lin'an District between March and June 2024 through a stratified random survey of farm households operating at least 2 hectares (30 mu) of agricultural land. Of 360 distributed questionnaires, 326 valid responses were retained, a valid rate of 90.6 percent. The sample covers 12 townships and includes bamboo, nut, tea, and mixed-crop operations.

2.2 Variables

The dependent variable is the natural logarithm of household agricultural net income per capita in 2023. The key independent variable is the vertical integration index (VII), constructed from five binary items: whether the farm has a written sales contract, receives standardized inputs from a partner, adopts unified technical standards, participates in post-harvest processing, and sells under a partner's brand. Scores range from 0 to 5 and are normalized to 0–1. Organization model is coded as a categorical variable with three values: self-organized (reference), cooperative-led, and enterprise-led.

Control variables include farm size (log hectares), years of farming experience, education level, number of hired laborers, share of income from non-agricultural sources, access to credit, and township fixed effects.

2.3 Estimation strategy

An OLS model is first estimated:

ln(Income_i) = α + βVII_i + γModel_i + δX_i + μ_t + ε_i

where X is the vector of controls and μ_t denotes township fixed effects. Because farmers self-select into organization models, estimates may be biased by unobserved heterogeneity. Propensity score matching (PSM) is therefore applied, using nearest-neighbor matching with a caliper of 0.05 to compare integrated and non-integrated farms with similar observable characteristics. Balancing tests confirm that standardized biases after matching fall below 10 percent.

3. Results and Analysis

3.1 Descriptive statistics

The average vertical integration index is 0.42. Enterprise-led farms record the highest mean index (0.68), followed by cooperative-led farms (0.51) and self-organized farms (0.23). Mean per capita agricultural net income is 28,640 yuan for enterprise-led farms, 23,180 yuan for cooperative-led farms, and 17,450 yuan for self-organized farms. Farm size does not differ significantly across the three groups (F = 1.87, p = 0.16), suggesting that organization rather than scale drives the gap.

3.2 Regression results

The OLS estimates show that a one-unit increase in the vertical integration index raises per capita agricultural income by approximately 34.6 percent (β = 0.297, p < 0.01). Relative to self-organized farms, cooperative-led participation adds 18.2 percent (p < 0.05) and enterprise-led participation adds 27.9 percent (p < 0.01). Farm size is positive and significant (β = 0.113, p < 0.05), but its marginal effect is smaller than that of integration. Education and credit access are also positively associated with income.

3.3 Matching results

After PSM, the average treatment effect on the treated for vertical integration is 0.241 (t = 3.42), equivalent to roughly 27 percent higher income. The effect for enterprise-led participation (0.263) exceeds that for cooperative-led participation (0.164). These results are robust to trimming the sample at the 5th and 95th percentiles and to using kernel matching.

3.4 Mechanisms

Mediation analysis indicates three channels. First, integrated farms pay 8–12 percent less for seed, fertilizer, and feed due to bulk procurement. Second, they receive an average price premium of 11 percent, chiefly through brand and grade-based sales. Third, their income volatility, measured by the coefficient of variation over three years, is 22 percent lower, reflecting reduced exposure to spot-market swings.

4. Discussion

The findings support the view that vertical integration, not land scale per se, is the more reliable driver of income growth for large-scale farmers. The superiority of enterprise-led models likely reflects stronger capital backing, more demanding quality standards, and access to longer value chains. Cooperative-led models perform well but are constrained by limited processing capacity and uneven member commitment.

Three qualifications deserve attention. First, integration may entail dependence and lock-in, and unequal bargaining power within contracts can erode gains over time. Second, the cross-sectional design cannot fully rule out reverse causality, since more profitable farms may be more attractive partners. Third, Lin'an's proximity to Hangzhou confers market access that less favored regions may lack, limiting external validity.

Policy implications follow. Governments should support contract enforcement and dispute resolution, strengthen cooperatives' processing and marketing functions, and provide technical assistance that helps farmers meet the quality standards required by enterprise partners. Simply enlarging farms without corresponding organizational linkage is unlikely to deliver sustained income growth.

5. Conclusion

This study uses survey data from 326 large-scale farmers in Lin'an to examine the relationship between organization model, vertical integration, and income growth. The evidence indicates that vertical integration raises per capita agricultural income by roughly 27 to 35 percent, with enterprise-led models outperforming cooperative-led and self-organized arrangements. The effects operate through lower input costs, price premiums, and reduced income volatility. These results suggest that deepening vertical linkages should be a priority in policies aimed at raising the incomes of large-scale farmers in China's peri-urban agricultural regions.

title: China's greenhouse gas emissions for cropping systems from 1978-2016
text:
Agriculture is a major contributor to global anthropogenic greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, accounting for roughly 10–12% of the total, with cropland management, enteric fermentation, and fertilizer use among the principal sources. As the world's most populous country and largest agricultural producer, China plays a pivotal role in the global GHG budget. Since the launch of economic reforms in 1978, Chinese agriculture has undergone profound transformations: grain output has more than doubled, chemical fertilizer consumption has risen several-fold, and mechanization, irrigation, and cropping intensity have expanded rapidly. These changes have substantially altered the magnitude and composition of GHG emissions from cropping systems, yet the long-term trajectories and underlying drivers remain insufficiently quantified.

Existing studies have either focused on short time spans, single gases, or individual regions, and often rely on coarse emission factors that fail to capture the heterogeneity of China's diverse agro-ecological zones and management practices. Consequently, estimates of the magnitude, spatial patterns, and temporal trends of emissions from Chinese cropping systems vary widely, hampering both scientific understanding and policy formulation. A consistent, long-term, and spatially explicit accounting of GHG emissions is therefore urgently needed to identify mitigation opportunities and to track progress toward national climate commitments, including China's pledge to peak carbon emissions before 2030 and achieve carbon neutrality by 2060.

Here we present a comprehensive assessment of GHG emissions from China's cropping systems over the period 1978–2016. We compiled province-level activity data on major crops, fertilizer application, rice cultivation, and residue burning, and combined them with region-specific emission factors to estimate emissions of carbon dioxide, methane, and nitrous oxide. Our objectives are threefold: (1) to reconstruct the temporal dynamics and spatial distribution of GHG emissions from cropping systems; (2) to disentangle the contributions of different crops, gases, and management practices; and (3) to explore the socio-economic and agronomic drivers underlying these trends. By providing a long-term, spatially resolved emission inventory, this study offers a scientific basis for designing targeted mitigation strategies and for evaluating the environmental consequences of agricultural intensification in China.

title: Development of an RNA-protein crosslinker to capture protein interactions with diverse RNA structures in cells
text:
Results and Discussion

We developed RNA-protein crosslinker (RPC) 12, a bifunctional reagent coupling a uridine-binding moiety to a photoactivatable diazirine. RPC-12 labeled 87% of tested RNA structures in vitro, including hairpins, G-quadruplexes, and pseudoknots, with minimal sequence bias. In HEK293T cells, UV activation (365 nm, 5 min) yielded 4.2-fold higher crosslink efficiency than formaldehyde and captured 1,863 high-confidence RNA-protein interactions, 71% of which were absent from PAR-CLIP datasets. Validation by western blot confirmed capture of known binders (e.g., PTBP1, 6.8-fold enrichment) alongside 14 novel interactions. Notably, 23% of crosslinks mapped to structured non-coding regions previously refractory to CLIP-based methods. Crosslinking showed modest cytotoxicity (92% viability at 24 h), supporting applicability to primary cells. These results establish RPC-12 as a broadly enabling tool for interrogating RNA-protein interactions across diverse RNA structures in living cells.

title: Contribution of High-Pressure-Induced Protein Modifications to the Microenvironment and Functional Properties of Rabbit Meat Sausages
text:
Contribution of High-Pressure-Induced Protein Modifications to the Microenvironment and Functional Properties of Rabbit Meat Sausages

Abstract

This study investigated the effects of high-pressure processing (HPP) at different intensity levels (100, 200, 300, and 400 MPa) on the protein structure, microenvironment, and functional properties of rabbit meat sausages. Protein modifications were characterized by surface hydrophobicity, sulfhydryl content, secondary structure, and particle size distribution. Results showed that HPP at 200–300 MPa significantly increased surface hydrophobicity and reduced total sulfhydryl content, indicating partial unfolding of myofibrillar proteins and exposure of buried hydrophobic groups. Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy revealed a decrease in α-helix content and an increase in β-sheet and random coil structures. These conformational changes enhanced water-holding capacity (WHC), gel strength, and emulsifying stability, with the 300 MPa treatment yielding the most favorable textural and microstructural properties. However, excessive pressure (400 MPa) induced protein aggregation, leading to reduced WHC and deteriorated gel network. The microenvironment alternations, including increased local hydrophobicity and altered electrostatic interactions, were closely associated with improved functional performance. This study provides a mechanistic understanding of HPP-induced protein modifications in rabbit meat sausages and supports the application of HPP as a non-thermal strategy to improve product quality.

Keywords: high-pressure processing; rabbit meat sausage; protein modification; microenvironment; gel properties; water-holding capacity

1. Introduction

Rabbit meat is recognized as a high-quality protein source with low fat, low cholesterol, and a favorable amino acid profile. However, its processing into emulsified meat products such as sausages remains challenging due to the relatively weak gelation capacity of rabbit myofibrillar proteins and their sensitivity to thermal treatment. Conventional heating often leads to excessive cooking loss and poor texture. Therefore, non-thermal or mild processing technologies that can modify protein functionality are of increasing interest.

High-pressure processing (HPP) is a non-thermal technology that applies hydrostatic pressure (100–600 MPa) to food systems, inducing conformational changes in proteins without significantly affecting small molecules such as vitamins and flavor compounds. HPP can disrupt non-covalent interactions (hydrogen bonds, hydrophobic interactions, and electrostatic forces), leading to protein unfolding, aggregation, or gelation depending on pressure intensity, temperature, and holding time. In meat systems, HPP has been shown to improve water-holding capacity (WHC), texture, and emulsifying properties. However, the relationship between HPP-induced protein modifications, the local microenvironment (e.g., hydrophobicity and charge distribution), and the functional properties of rabbit meat sausages has not been systematically elucidated.

The objective of this study was to evaluate the contribution of HPP-induced protein modifications to the microenvironment and functional properties of rabbit meat sausages. We hypothesized that moderate HPP would partially unfold myofibrillar proteins, expose hydrophobic and sulfhydryl groups, and thereby enhance gel network formation and WHC, while excessive pressure would cause irreversible aggregation and quality deterioration. The findings aim to provide a theoretical basis for optimizing HPP conditions in rabbit meat product development.

2. Materials and Methods

2.1 Materials

Fresh rabbit hind leg meat (24 h post-mortem) was obtained from a local commercial slaughterhouse. Visible fat and connective tissue were removed. Rabbit backfat, sodium chloride, sodium nitrite, and sodium tripolyphosphate were of food grade. All chemicals for analysis were of analytical grade.

2.2 Sausage Preparation

Lean rabbit meat (70%) and backfat (20%) were chopped with ice water (10%) and additives (2.5% NaCl, 0.01% sodium nitrite, 0.3% sodium tripolyphosphate). The batter was stuffed into collagen casings (diameter 22 mm) and vacuum-sealed. Samples were randomly assigned to five groups: control (0.1 MPa, no HPP) and HPP at 100, 200, 300, and 400 MPa.

2.3 High-Pressure Processing

HPP was performed using a laboratory-scale high-pressure unit (Wuhan, China) with water as the pressure-transmitting medium. The pressure was increased at ~100 MPa/min, held for 10 min at 4 °C, and released within 30 s. After HPP, all sausages were heated in a water bath at 80 °C for 30 min to reach a core temperature of 72 °C, then cooled to 4 °C overnight before analysis.

2.4 Protein Microenvironment Analysis

Surface hydrophobicity was determined using 1-anilinonaphthalene-8-sulfonic acid (ANS) as a fluorescent probe. Total sulfhydryl content was measured using Ellman’s reagent. Secondary structure was analyzed by Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) in the amide I region (1600–1700 cm⁻¹) with peak deconvolution. Particle size distribution was measured by dynamic light scattering. Zeta potential was determined to assess surface charge.

2.5 Functional Properties

Water-holding capacity (WHC) was expressed as the percentage of water retained after centrifugation. Gel strength was measured using a texture analyzer with a cylindrical probe. Emulsifying activity index (EAI) and emulsifying stability index (ESI) were determined by turbidimetry. Cooking loss was calculated from weight differences before and after heating.

2.6 Microstructure

Microstructure was observed using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) at 10 kV. Samples were fixed, dehydrated, critical-point dried, and gold-coated.

2.7 Statistical Analysis

All experiments were performed in triplicate. Data were analyzed by one-way ANOVA followed by Duncan’s multiple range test (P < 0.05) using SPSS 22.0.

3. Results and Analysis

3.1 Protein Microenvironment Changes

Surface hydrophobicity increased significantly from 42.3 (control) to 78.6 at 300 MPa (P < 0.05), then decreased to 65.2 at 400 MPa. Total sulfhydryl content decreased from 68.4 μmol/g to 45.2 μmol/g at 300 MPa, indicating oxidation and exposure of sulfhydryl groups. Zeta potential became less negative with increasing pressure up to 300 MPa (−28.4 mV to −18.6 mV), suggesting reduced electrostatic repulsion and enhanced hydrophobic interactions.

FTIR analysis showed that α-helix content decreased from 38.5% (control) to 24.1% at 300 MPa, while β-sheet and random coil increased from 32.1% and 18.2% to 41.3% and 26.7%, respectively. Particle size increased from 120 nm to 280 nm at 300 MPa, but further increased to 450 nm at 400 MPa, indicating aggregation.

3.2 Functional Properties

WHC increased from 72.5% (control) to 88.3% at 300 MPa, then decreased to 79.1% at 400 MPa. Gel strength followed a similar trend, peaking at 300 MPa (2.45 N) compared to control (1.32 N). Cooking loss was lowest at 300 MPa (6.8%) versus control (12.4%). EAI and ESI were highest at 200–300 MPa, with values of 18.6 m²/g and 92.4 min, respectively, compared to 12.3 m²/g and 65.2 min for the control.

3.3 Microstructure

SEM images revealed that control sausages had a coarse and discontinuous gel network with large pores. At 200–300 MPa, the network became denser, more uniform, and with smaller pores, consistent with improved WHC and gel strength. At 400 MPa, large protein aggregates disrupted the network, resulting in irregular cavities.

4. Discussion

The results demonstrate that HPP-induced protein modifications play a critical role in determining the microenvironment and functional properties of rabbit meat sausages. Moderate pressure (200–300 MPa) partially unfolds myofibrillar proteins, exposing buried hydrophobic and sulfhydryl groups. This unfolding increases surface hydrophobicity and reduces electrostatic repulsion, promoting hydrophobic interactions and disulfide bond formation between protein molecules. These changes facilitate the formation of a fine, dense gel network that entraps water more effectively, thereby improving WHC, gel strength, and emulsifying stability.

The decrease in α-helix and increase in β-sheet and random coil structures are consistent with pressure-induced unfolding and subsequent aggregation. The exposed hydrophobic groups can interact with fat globules, enhancing emulsifying properties. However, excessive pressure (400 MPa) causes irreversible aggregation, leading to oversized protein particles that disrupt the gel network and reduce WHC. This threshold behavior is in agreement with previous studies on pork and fish myofibrillar proteins.

The microenvironmental changes, particularly increased local hydrophobicity and altered charge distribution, are key mediators of the functional improvements. The reduced zeta potential at 300 MPa indicates that electrostatic repulsion is minimized, allowing proteins to approach and interact more closely. This is beneficial for gelation but must be balanced against excessive aggregation.

From a practical perspective, HPP at 300 MPa for 10 min at 4 °C appears optimal for rabbit meat sausages, improving texture and yield without compromising product quality. The study also suggests that HPP can be used as a pre-treatment before heating to enhance protein functionality, potentially reducing the need for phosphate additives.

5. Conclusion

This study demonstrated that high-pressure processing at 200–300 MPa significantly modifies the microenvironment of rabbit meat proteins by increasing surface hydrophobicity, reducing sulfhydryl content, and altering secondary structure. These modifications enhance water-holding capacity, gel strength, and emulsifying properties, leading to improved quality of rabbit meat sausages. Excessive pressure (400 MPa) induces protein aggregation and deteriorates gel network. The optimal HPP condition was 300 MPa for 10 min at 4 °C. The findings provide a mechanistic basis for applying HPP as a non-thermal processing strategy to improve the functional properties of rabbit meat products.

title: Can machine learning predict drug nanocrystals?
text:
Can machine learning predict drug nanocrystals?

 Abstract

Drug nanocrystals have emerged as a versatile formulation strategy for poorly soluble drugs, yet their development remains largely empirical. This study investigated whether machine learning (ML) models can predict nanocrystal formation and resulting particle size from molecular and process descriptors. A dataset of 240 experimental records was compiled, encompassing 40 active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) and six processing methods. Three algorithms—random forest (RF), gradient boosting (GB), and artificial neural network (ANN)—were trained to classify successful nanocrystal formation and to regress mean particle size. GB achieved the best classification performance (accuracy = 0.89, AUC = 0.93), while ANN predicted particle size most accurately (R² = 0.84, RMSE = 38 nm). Molecular descriptors (logP, melting point, molecular weight) dominated feature importance, with process parameters contributing secondarily. These findings suggest that ML can serve as a rational screening tool for nanocrystal formulation, though prospective validation on external compounds is required.

Keywords: nanocrystals; machine learning; poorly soluble drugs; particle size prediction; formulation informatics

 1. Introduction

Approximately 70% of new chemical entities suffer from poor aqueous solubility, limiting oral bioavailability. Drug nanocrystals—nanosized pure drug particles stabilized by surfactants or polymers—address this challenge by increasing dissolution velocity without altering molecular structure. Production methods include top-down approaches (wet media milling, high-pressure homogenization) and bottom-up approaches (antisolvent precipitation, spray drying).

Despite widespread use, nanocrystal development remains trial-and-error. Whether a given API will successfully form stable nanocrystals, and at what size, depends on a complex interplay of molecular properties, stabilizer selection, and process energy. Machine learning offers a route to extract patterns from historical formulation data, potentially reducing experimental burden. However, few studies have systematically tested ML for nanocrystal prediction. This work addresses the question: can ML predict drug nanocrystals?

 2. Materials and Methods

 2.1 Dataset

A retrospective dataset of 240 formulation records was assembled from laboratory archives (2018–2023), covering 40 APIs (e.g., ibuprofen, fenofibrate, griseofulvin, curcumin, ritonavir). Each record included:

- Molecular descriptors: molecular weight (MW), logP, melting point (Tm), topological polar surface area (TPSA), number of rotatable bonds.
- Process parameters: production method (media milling, HPH, antisolvent precipitation, sonoprecipitation, spray drying, microfluidization), drug concentration (1–50 mg/mL), stabilizer type (HPMC, PVP, SDS, poloxamer), stabilizer-to-drug ratio (0.2–2.0), milling time or homogenization cycles.
- Outcomes: binary formation success (defined as particles <1000 nm with PDI <0.3 and no aggregation at 24 h) and mean particle size (Z-average, nm).

Success rate was 68% (163/240). Mean particle size across successful runs was 212 ± 96 nm.

 2.2 Data Preprocessing

Categorical variables were one-hot encoded. Features were standardized (z-score). The dataset was split 70/15/15 into training, validation, and test sets, stratified by outcome. SMOTE was applied to the training set to address class imbalance.

 2.3 Model Development

Three algorithms were implemented in Python (scikit-learn, TensorFlow): random forest (500 trees), gradient boosting (learning rate 0.05, 300 estimators), and a feedforward ANN (two hidden layers: 64 and 32 neurons, ReLU activation, dropout 0.2, Adam optimizer). Classification models were evaluated by accuracy, precision, recall, F1, and AUC. Regression models (particle size) were evaluated by R² and RMSE. Five-fold cross-validation was performed. Feature importance was assessed via permutation analysis.

 3. Results

 3.1 Classification of Nanocrystal Formation

GB outperformed other models on the held-out test set (Table 1). All models exceeded 80% accuracy, substantially above the 68% baseline.

Table 1. Classification performance (test set, n = 36)

| Model | Accuracy | Precision | Recall | F1 | AUC |
|-------|----------|-----------|--------|-----|-----|
| RF | 0.86 | 0.88 | 0.89 | 0.88 | 0.90 |
| GB | 0.89 | 0.91 | 0.90 | 0.90 | 0.93 |
| ANN | 0.83 | 0.85 | 0.86 | 0.85 | 0.88 |

 3.2 Prediction of Particle Size

ANN regression achieved R² = 0.84 (RMSE = 38 nm) on the test set, versus R² = 0.76 (RMSE = 47 nm) for GB and R² = 0.71 (RMSE = 52 nm) for RF. Predicted versus actual sizes showed slight underestimation for particles >350 nm.

 3.3 Feature Importance

Permutation importance ranked logP (0.21), Tm (0.18), MW (0.14), stabilizer-to-drug ratio (0.12), and production method (0.10) as the top predictors. High logP (>4) and Tm (>200 °C) were associated with reduced success probability, consistent with poor wetting and high crystal lattice energy.

 4. Discussion

The results support the hypothesis that ML can predict nanocrystal outcomes with useful accuracy. GB's classification strength likely reflects its robustness to correlated descriptors and mixed data types. The ANN's superior size regression suggests nonlinear structure–size relationships that tree ensembles partially miss.

The dominance of molecular descriptors aligns with nucleation theory: crystallization propensity depends on solubility and lattice energy, captured by logP and Tm. Process parameters mattered most within a given API, echoing prior reports that stabilizer ratio and energy input govern final size.

Several limitations warrant mention. The dataset is modest (240 records) and unbalanced across APIs, risking overfitting to well-represented compounds. Success definitions are operational rather than mechanistic. No external validation set was used; performance on novel scaffolds may be lower. Additionally, unmeasured factors (impurities, temperature, stirring geometry) introduce noise.

Despite these caveats, the models offer practical value as pre-screening tools: flagging APIs unlikely to form nanocrystals and suggesting process windows. Future work should integrate molecular dynamics descriptors, expand to multi-lab datasets, and prospectively test predictions on 10–20 new compounds.

 5. Conclusion

Machine learning models predicted drug nanocrystal formation with up to 89% accuracy and particle size with R² = 0.84 using only readily available molecular and process descriptors. Gradient boosting proved best for classification, while neural networks excelled at size regression. Molecular properties—particularly logP and melting point—were the strongest predictors. ML is not yet a replacement for experimental formulation science, but it can meaningfully prioritize candidates and reduce development cycles. Prospective validation remains the essential next step.

title: Perceived Factors Influencing the Public Intention to Use E-Consultation: Analysis of Web-Based Survey Data
text: Abstract: E-consultation has emerged as a promising channel for public participation in health care decision-making, yet its adoption remains limited. This study aimed to identify perceived factors influencing the public intention to use e-consultation. A web-based survey was conducted, and data from valid respondents were analyzed using structural equation modeling. The results showed that perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, and trust in e-consultation significantly and positively affected usage intention, while perceived risk exerted a negative influence. Social influence also played a significant role in shaping intention. Notably, perceived usefulness mediated the relationships between ease of use, trust, and usage intention. These findings suggest that improving system usability, building public trust, reducing perceived risks, and leveraging social influence are essential for promoting e-consultation adoption. The study provides theoretical and practical implications for health-care providers and policymakers seeking to enhance public engagement through digital platforms.

title: Influencing factors of self-directed learning abilities of medical students of mainland China: a cross-sectional study
text:
Influencing factors of self-directed learning abilities of medical students of mainland China: a cross-sectional study

Abstract

Background: Self-directed learning (SDL) ability is an essential competency for medical students, particularly under the current competency-based medical education framework. However, the levels and determinants of SDL ability among medical students in mainland China remain insufficiently characterized. This study aimed to evaluate the current status of SDL ability and identify its influencing factors among medical students in mainland China.

Methods: A cross-sectional survey was conducted between March and May 2024 in five medical universities located in eastern, central, and western China. A total of 1,286 medical students were recruited using stratified cluster random sampling. Data were collected using a sociodemographic questionnaire and the Self-Directed Learning Ability Scale for Medical Students (SDLAMS), which includes four dimensions: learning motivation, planning and implementation, self-monitoring, and interpersonal communication. Multivariate linear regression was performed to identify factors associated with SDL ability.

Results: The mean total SDL ability score was 3.62 ± 0.58 (out of 5). The highest dimension score was learning motivation (3.91 ± 0.63), while the lowest was self-monitoring (3.31 ± 0.71). Multivariate regression analysis showed that gender (β = 0.118, P < 0.001), academic year (β = -0.094, P = 0.002), participation in scientific research (β = 0.156, P < 0.001), frequency of online learning (β = 0.132, P < 0.001), teacher feedback (β = 0.141, P < 0.001), and academic self-efficacy (β = 0.287, P < 0.001) were significant predictors of SDL ability, explaining 36.4% of the total variance.

Conclusions: The SDL ability of medical students in mainland China is at a moderate-to-upper level, with self-monitoring being the weakest dimension. Gender, academic year, research participation, online learning frequency, teacher feedback, and academic self-efficacy significantly influence SDL ability. Targeted interventions should be designed to strengthen self-monitoring skills, promote early research exposure, and enhance teacher feedback and academic self-efficacy.

Keywords: self-directed learning; medical students; influencing factors; cross-sectional study; mainland China; medical education

1. Introduction

Self-directed learning (SDL) refers to the process in which learners take the initiative to diagnose their learning needs, formulate learning goals, select appropriate learning resources and strategies, and evaluate learning outcomes (Knowles, 1975). In medical education, SDL has become increasingly important because medical knowledge expands rapidly and clinical competence requires lifelong learning. The Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education and many national medical education standards have incorporated SDL as a core competency. In China, the "Standard for Basic Medical Education" issued by the Ministry of Education explicitly requires medical schools to cultivate students' autonomous learning abilities.

Previous studies have reported that SDL ability is associated with various individual and environmental factors, including gender, age, academic performance, learning environment, teacher support, and internet use. However, most studies have been conducted in Western countries, and findings may not be directly generalizable to Chinese medical students, who study in a highly examination-oriented and teacher-centered educational culture. Moreover, few studies have simultaneously examined psychological, behavioral, and pedagogical factors using a large multi-center sample.

Therefore, this study aimed to: (1) describe the current level of SDL ability among medical students in mainland China; and (2) identify sociodemographic, behavioral, and educational factors associated with SDL ability. The findings may provide evidence for designing effective educational interventions.

2. Materials and Methods

2.1 Study design and participants

A cross-sectional study was conducted from March to May 2024. Five medical universities were selected from eastern (Shanghai, Jiangsu), central (Hubei), and western (Sichuan, Shaanxi) China. Eligible participants were full-time undergraduate medical students in years 1–5. Stratified cluster random sampling was used, with academic year as the stratification variable and class as the cluster unit. Students with incomplete questionnaires or who refused participation were excluded. The study was approved by the Ethics Committee of the lead university (approval no. 2024-031). Informed consent was obtained from all participants.

2.2 Sample size

Based on a conservative expected proportion of 50%, a 95% confidence level, and a 3% margin of error, the minimum required sample size was 1,067. Considering a 20% non-response rate, 1,350 students were invited, and 1,286 valid questionnaires were returned (valid response rate 95.3%).

2.3 Instruments

A three-part questionnaire was used.

(1) Sociodemographic and behavioral information: age, gender, academic year, residence (urban/rural), only-child status, parental education, monthly living expenses, participation in scientific research, frequency of online learning, and frequency of teacher feedback.

(2) Self-Directed Learning Ability Scale for Medical Students (SDLAMS): This 24-item scale was adapted from previous validated instruments and included four dimensions: learning motivation (6 items), planning and implementation (7 items), self-monitoring (6 items), and interpersonal communication (5 items). Each item was rated on a 5-point Likert scale (1 = strongly disagree, 5 = strongly agree). The overall Cronbach's α was 0.912, and subscale α values ranged from 0.781 to 0.876. Confirmatory factor analysis showed acceptable fit (CFI = 0.931, RMSEA = 0.058).

(3) Academic Self-Efficacy Scale: A 10-item scale was used, with a Cronbach's α of 0.889.

2.4 Data collection

Questionnaires were distributed online via a secure platform during regular class meetings. Trained research assistants explained the purpose and anonymity of the survey. Participants completed the questionnaire independently within 20 minutes.

2.5 Statistical analysis

Data were analyzed using SPSS 26.0. Continuous variables were presented as mean ± standard deviation, and categorical variables as frequencies and percentages. Independent-sample t-tests and one-way ANOVA were used for univariate analysis. Pearson correlation was used to examine relationships between continuous variables. Multivariate linear regression with stepwise entry was performed to identify independent factors associated with SDL ability. Statistical significance was set at P < 0.05 (two-tailed).

3. Results and Analysis

3.1 Participant characteristics

A total of 1,286 medical students were included. The mean age was 21.3 ± 2.1 years. There were 562 males (43.7%) and 724 females (56.3%). Students in years 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5 accounted for 21.2%, 20.8%, 20.1%, 19.4%, and 18.5%, respectively. Urban residents comprised 58.9%, and 41.1% were from rural areas. Only 27.6% had participated in scientific research, and 62.3% reported using online learning resources at least three times per week. Frequent teacher feedback was reported by 45.8% of students.

3.2 Level of SDL ability

The mean total SDL ability score was 3.62 ± 0.58. Dimension scores were as follows: learning motivation 3.91 ± 0.63, planning and implementation 3.68 ± 0.61, interpersonal communication 3.57 ± 0.66, and self-monitoring 3.31 ± 0.71. The lowest-scoring item was "I can regularly evaluate whether my learning methods are effective" (3.12 ± 0.82).

3.3 Univariate analysis

Female students scored higher than male students (3.68 ± 0.56 vs. 3.54 ± 0.60, P < 0.001). Students who participated in scientific research scored higher than those who did not (3.81 ± 0.55 vs. 3.55 ± 0.59, P < 0.001). Students with frequent online learning scored higher than infrequent users (3.74 ± 0.56 vs. 3.48 ± 0.60, P < 0.001). Students receiving frequent teacher feedback scored higher than those receiving rare feedback (3.79 ± 0.54 vs. 3.49 ± 0.60, P < 0.001). Academic self-efficacy was positively correlated with SDL ability (r = 0.512, P < 0.001). Academic year showed a nonlinear pattern: year 1 students scored 3.58 ± 0.59, year 2 3.66 ± 0.57, year 3 3.71 ± 0.56, year 4 3.60 ± 0.58, and year 5 3.52 ± 0.61 (P = 0.008).

3.4 Multivariate linear regression

The regression model was significant (F = 48.62, P < 0.001) and explained 36.4% of the variance in SDL ability (adjusted R² = 0.358). Significant predictors were: academic self-efficacy (β = 0.287, P < 0.001), participation in scientific research (β = 0.156, P < 0.001), teacher feedback (β = 0.141, P < 0.001), online learning frequency (β = 0.132, P < 0.001), gender (female) (β = 0.118, P < 0.001), and academic year (β = -0.094, P = 0.002). Residence, only-child status, parental education, and monthly living expenses were not significant (P > 0.05).

4. Discussion

This study found that medical students in mainland China had a moderate-to-upper level of SDL ability, which is consistent with some previous Chinese studies but slightly lower than findings from some Western cohorts. The relatively weak self-monitoring dimension is concerning because self-monitoring is critical for identifying learning gaps and adjusting strategies. This weakness may reflect the long-standing examination-oriented culture in Chinese medical education, where external evaluation by teachers and examinations dominates, leaving students with limited opportunities to practice self-assessment.

The positive association between academic self-efficacy and SDL ability is consistent with social cognitive theory. Students who believe in their capacity to succeed are more likely to set challenging goals, persist in the face of difficulties, and use self-regulatory strategies. This suggests that interventions aimed at enhancing self-efficacy, such as mastery experiences, verbal persuasion, and vicarious learning, may indirectly improve SDL.

Participation in scientific research was a strong predictor of SDL ability. Research activities require students to formulate questions, search literature, design methods, and interpret data, all of which are core SDL behaviors. Early exposure to research may therefore foster autonomous learning habits. Medical schools should consider integrating research training into the undergraduate curriculum, especially in early years.

The positive role of teacher feedback supports the idea that SDL does not mean learning in isolation. Effective feedback provides direction, reduces uncertainty, and helps students calibrate their learning. In the Chinese context, where teacher authority remains high, feedback may be particularly influential. Faculty development programs should train teachers to provide timely, specific, and constructive feedback.

Online learning frequency was also positively associated with SDL ability. The internet offers abundant resources and flexibility, but it also requires self-discipline. Students who frequently use online learning may develop better planning and monitoring skills. However, the cross-sectional design cannot exclude reverse causality.

Female students scored higher than male students, which may be related to differences in learning attitudes, compliance, and self-regulation. The decline in SDL ability in later academic years may be due to increased clinical workload, examination pressure, and fatigue, which reduce opportunities for self-directed learning. This finding highlights the need to sustain SDL training throughout the medical curriculum, not only in pre-clinical years.

This study has several limitations. First, the cross-sectional design precludes causal inference. Second, self-reported data may be subject to social desirability bias. Third, although five universities were included, the sample may not represent all medical students in mainland China. Fourth, unmeasured factors such as personality traits and learning environment may confound the results. Future longitudinal and mixed-methods studies are warranted.

5. Conclusion

The SDL ability of medical students in mainland China is at a moderate-to-upper level, with self-monitoring being the weakest dimension. Academic self-efficacy, participation in scientific research, teacher feedback, online learning frequency, gender, and academic year are significant influencing factors. Medical educators should design targeted interventions to strengthen self-monitoring, promote early research engagement, enhance teacher feedback, and foster academic self-efficacy. These efforts may help cultivate lifelong learning competencies required for modern medical practice.

title: Effect of optimal daily fertigation on migration of water and salt in soil, root growth and fruit yield of cucumber (Cucumis sativus L.) in solar-greenhouse
text: Solar-greenhouse vegetable production in China is often characterized by excessive irrigation and fertilizer application, which leads to shallow root distribution, secondary soil salinization, and reduced crop productivity. Cucumber (Cucumis sativus L.) is one of the most important greenhouse vegetables, yet its yield and quality are highly sensitive to water and salt dynamics in the root zone. Fertigation, the combined application of water and soluble fertilizers through drip systems, has been widely adopted to improve water and nutrient use efficiency. However, the effects of daily fertigation at optimal rates on soil water and salt migration, root growth, and fruit yield remain insufficiently quantified, particularly under the unique microclimate and soil conditions of solar-greenhouses. Most previous studies have focused on irrigation frequency or fertilizer concentration separately, and few have integrated soil physical processes with crop physiological responses. Therefore, a two-season experiment was conducted to investigate how optimal daily fertigation influences water and salt distribution in the soil profile, root architecture, and cucumber fruit yield in a solar-greenhouse. The results are expected to provide a theoretical basis for precision water and fertilizer management in protected cucumber production.

title: Investigating the effect of nitrate on juvenile turbot (Scophthalmus maximus) growth performance, health status, and endocrine function in marine recirculation aquaculture systems
text:
Results and Discussion

After 60 days, nitrate exposure significantly impaired turbot growth. Final body weight decreased from 214.3 ± 9.8 g (control, 12 mg/L NO₃⁻-N) to 168.7 ± 11.2 g at 250 mg/L and 141.5 ± 10.4 g at 500 mg/L (p < 0.01), with specific growth rates falling from 1.42 to 0.98 and 0.81 %/day, respectively. Feed conversion ratio increased from 0.89 to 1.18 at the highest exposure. Plasma cortisol rose from 8.4 ± 2.1 ng/mL to 26.7 ± 4.3 ng/mL, while triiodothyronine (T3) declined from 3.8 ± 0.4 to 2.1 ± 0.3 ng/mL, indicating disrupted endocrine function. Hematocrit and lysozyme activity were also reduced at ≥250 mg/L. These results demonstrate that chronic nitrate exposure above 125 mg/L compromises growth, stress physiology, and immune status of juvenile turbot, suggesting that RAS operators should maintain nitrate below this threshold.

title: Antioxidant mechanism of tea polyphenols and its impact on health benefits
text:
Antioxidant Mechanism of Tea Polyphenols and Its Impact on Health Benefits

Abstract

Tea polyphenols, a group of bioactive compounds abundant in Camellia sinensis, have attracted considerable attention due to their potent antioxidant properties and associated health-promoting effects. This study aimed to elucidate the antioxidant mechanisms of tea polyphenols and evaluate their impact on human health. Using in vitro assays and a randomized controlled trial involving 120 healthy adults, we assessed the radical-scavenging capacity, metal-chelating activity, and modulation of endogenous antioxidant enzymes by tea polyphenol extracts. Results showed that tea polyphenols exhibited strong DPPH and ABTS radical-scavenging activities (IC50 = 18.4 ± 1.2 μg/mL and 12.7 ± 0.9 μg/mL, respectively), significant ferrous ion chelation (76.3% ± 3.1%), and enhanced activities of superoxide dismutase (SOD), catalase (CAT), and glutathione peroxidase (GPx) in vivo. After 12 weeks of supplementation, serum malondialdehyde (MDA) decreased by 28.5%, while total antioxidant capacity increased by 34.2%. Furthermore, improvements in lipid profiles and inflammatory markers were observed. These findings suggest that tea polyphenols exert antioxidant effects through multiple pathways, including direct radical scavenging, metal chelation, and upregulation of endogenous antioxidant defense systems, thereby contributing to cardiovascular and metabolic health benefits.

Keywords: tea polyphenols; antioxidant mechanism; oxidative stress; health benefits; epigallocatechin gallate

1. Introduction

Oxidative stress, arising from an imbalance between reactive oxygen species (ROS) and antioxidant defense, is implicated in the pathogenesis of numerous chronic diseases, including cardiovascular disease, diabetes, cancer, and neurodegenerative disorders (Halliwell, 2007). Dietary antioxidants have thus gained prominence as potential preventive agents. Tea, consumed worldwide, is rich in polyphenols, particularly catechins such as epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG), epicatechin gallate (ECG), and epigallocatechin (EGC). These compounds possess a flavan-3-ol skeleton with multiple hydroxyl groups, conferring strong electron-donating capacity.

The antioxidant mechanisms of tea polyphenols are multifaceted. Direct mechanisms include scavenging free radicals and chelating transition metal ions. Indirect mechanisms involve modulation of transcription factors (e.g., Nrf2), inhibition of pro-oxidant enzymes (e.g., xanthine oxidase), and enhancement of endogenous antioxidant enzymes. Despite extensive research, a comprehensive understanding linking these mechanisms to concrete health outcomes remains incomplete. This study integrates in vitro and in vivo approaches to systematically evaluate the antioxidant mechanisms of tea polyphenols and their impact on health parameters.

2. Materials and Methods

2.1 Preparation of Tea Polyphenol Extract

Green tea leaves (Camellia sinensis) were extracted with 70% ethanol (1:20 w/v) at 60°C for 2 h. The extract was filtered, concentrated, and lyophilized. Total polyphenol content was determined by the Folin-Ciocalteu method, expressed as gallic acid equivalents (GAE). The extract contained 92.3% polyphenols, with EGCG comprising 48.7% of total catechins.

2.2 In Vitro Antioxidant Assays

DPPH and ABTS radical-scavenging activities were measured as described previously (Brand-Williams et al., 1995; Re et al., 1999). Ferrous ion chelation was assessed using the ferrozine method. All assays were performed in triplicate.

2.3 In Vivo Study Design

A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial was conducted with 120 healthy adults (aged 30–60 years) recruited from a local community. Participants were randomly assigned to either a tea polyphenol group (n=60; 500 mg/day) or placebo group (n=60) for 12 weeks. Exclusion criteria included smoking, chronic medication, and antioxidant supplementation. Blood samples were collected at baseline and week 12.

2.4 Biochemical Analyses

Serum MDA, SOD, CAT, GPx, total antioxidant capacity (TAC), lipid profile (total cholesterol, LDL-C, HDL-C, triglycerides), and inflammatory markers (IL-6, TNF-α) were measured using commercial kits.

2.5 Statistical Analysis

Data were expressed as mean ± SD. Comparisons between groups were performed using independent t-tests or ANOVA. A p-value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.

3. Results and Analysis

3.1 In Vitro Antioxidant Capacity

Tea polyphenol extract demonstrated potent radical-scavenging activity. IC50 values for DPPH and ABTS were 18.4 ± 1.2 μg/mL and 12.7 ± 0.9 μg/mL, respectively, comparable to ascorbic acid (IC50 = 15.2 ± 1.0 μg/mL for DPPH). Ferrous ion chelation was 76.3% ± 3.1% at 100 μg/mL, indicating strong metal-chelating ability.

3.2 Endogenous Antioxidant Enzyme Modulation

After 12 weeks, the tea polyphenol group showed significant increases in SOD (from 82.4 ± 6.7 to 112.6 ± 8.9 U/mL, p<0.01), CAT (from 45.2 ± 4.1 to 61.8 ± 5.3 U/mL, p<0.01), and GPx (from 120.5 ± 9.8 to 158.3 ± 11.2 U/mL, p<0.01). No significant changes were observed in the placebo group.

3.3 Oxidative Stress and Lipid Peroxidation

Serum MDA decreased by 28.5% in the tea polyphenol group (from 4.21 ± 0.45 to 3.01 ± 0.38 nmol/mL, p<0.001), while TAC increased by 34.2% (from 1.12 ± 0.09 to 1.50 ± 0.11 mmol Trolox equivalent/L, p<0.001). Placebo group showed no significant changes.

3.4 Lipid Profile and Inflammatory Markers

Tea polyphenol supplementation significantly reduced total cholesterol (−12.3%), LDL-C (−16.8%), and triglycerides (−14.5%), and increased HDL-C (+8.7%) (all p<0.05). IL-6 and TNF-α decreased by 22.4% and 18.9%, respectively (p<0.05).

4. Discussion

Our findings confirm that tea polyphenols exert antioxidant effects through direct and indirect mechanisms. The strong radical-scavenging and metal-chelating activities observed in vitro are attributable to the catechol structure of catechins, which donates hydrogen atoms or electrons to stabilize ROS. EGCG, the most abundant catechin, possesses eight hydroxyl groups, enhancing its antioxidant capacity.

In vivo, tea polyphenols upregulated SOD, CAT, and GPx, likely via activation of the Nrf2/ARE pathway, which induces expression of antioxidant response element-driven genes. This is consistent with previous reports (Na & Surh, 2008). The reduction in MDA, a marker of lipid peroxidation, and increased TAC reflect decreased oxidative damage.

The improvements in lipid profiles and inflammatory markers suggest that antioxidant mechanisms translate into systemic health benefits. Oxidized LDL is a key initiator of atherosclerosis; by inhibiting LDL oxidation and reducing inflammation, tea polyphenols may lower cardiovascular risk. However, limitations include the short intervention period and lack of bioavailability data. Future studies should measure plasma catechin metabolites and assess long-term outcomes.

5. Conclusion

Tea polyphenols exhibit robust antioxidant activity through multiple mechanisms: direct scavenging of free radicals, chelation of pro-oxidant metal ions, and enhancement of endogenous antioxidant enzymes. These actions collectively reduce oxidative stress, improve lipid profiles, and attenuate inflammation, contributing to cardiovascular and metabolic health benefits. Regular consumption of tea polyphenol-rich products may serve as a practical strategy to combat oxidative stress-related chronic diseases. Further research is warranted to elucidate molecular pathways and long-term clinical effects.

title: Assessment of internal exposure to methylsiloxanes in children and associated non-dietary exposure risk
text:
Assessment of internal exposure to methylsiloxanes in children and associated non-dietary exposure risk

 Abstract

Methylsiloxanes are widely used as emollients and carriers in personal care products (PCPs), yet data on children's internal exposure remain scarce. In this study, we measured five cyclic (D4–D6) and three linear (L5–L7) methylsiloxanes in urine and serum samples from 240 children (aged 3–12 years) residing in two urban regions, together with paired hand-wipe and indoor dust samples to characterize non-dietary exposure pathways. Urinary concentrations of Σmethylsiloxanes ranged from 12.4 to 486 ng/mL (geometric mean, GM = 74.6 ng/mL), with D5 and D4 dominating the profile. Serum Σmethylsiloxane levels (GM = 21.3 ng/mL) correlated significantly with urinary levels (r = 0.61, p < 0.01). Hand-wipe siloxane loads (GM = 3.82 μg/m²) and dust concentrations (GM = 18.7 μg/g) were significantly associated with urinary biomarkers, and dermal contact with PCPs was the strongest single predictor (β = 0.42, p < 0.001). Estimated daily intakes (EDI) of total methylsiloxanes via non-dietary routes ranged from 0.09 to 2.74 μg/kg-bw/day, remaining below provisional reference values; however, the hazard quotient for the 95th percentile of D5 exposure reached 0.68, indicating a narrow margin of safety. Our findings demonstrate that children experience measurable internal exposure to methylsiloxanes, primarily driven by dermal and hand-to-mouth transfer of PCP residues and indoor dust, and highlight the need for child-specific risk assessment and product regulation.

 Keywords

Methylsiloxanes; cyclic siloxanes; children; internal exposure; urine biomarkers; non-dietary exposure; indoor dust; risk assessment

 1. Introduction

Methylsiloxanes, including cyclic volatile methylsiloxanes (cVMS; D4, D5, D6) and linear volatile methylsiloxanes (lVMS; L5–L7), are high-production-volume chemicals used extensively as emollients, conditioners, and spreading agents in cosmetics, shampoos, lotions, and household products (Horii & Kannan, 2008). Because of their volatility, lipophilicity, and environmental persistence, D4 and D5 have been classified as substances of very high concern in some jurisdictions, with D4 identified as a potential endocrine disruptor and D5 suspected of reproductive toxicity.

Biomonitoring studies in adults have detected cVMS in serum, plasma, and adipose tissue, and more recently in urine, suggesting renal excretion of metabolites. However, children are a particularly susceptible subpopulation: they have higher surface-area-to-body-weight ratios, more frequent hand-to-mouth behaviors, thinner skin, and distinct product-use patterns (e.g., lotions, sunscreens, and play cosmetics), all of which may elevate non-dietary exposure. Despite this, data on internal methylsiloxane exposure in children remain limited, and most risk assessments rely on adult exposure parameters or external exposure estimates.

The objectives of this study were to: (i) quantify methylsiloxane concentrations in urine and serum of children; (ii) characterize paired non-dietary exposure sources including hand wipes, indoor dust, and PCP use; (iii) identify the main predictors of internal exposure; and (iv) estimate non-dietary exposure risks using a child-specific probabilistic approach.

 2. Materials and Methods

 2.1 Study population and sampling

A total of 240 children aged 3–12 years (mean age = 7.4 ± 2.6 years; 128 boys, 112 girls) were recruited from two urban regions (designated Region A and Region B) between March and June 2023 using a stratified random sampling strategy. Inclusion criteria required residence in the study area for ≥1 year and no known renal or hepatic disease. Written informed consent was obtained from parents or guardians, and verbal assent was obtained from children ≥7 years. The study was approved by the institutional ethics committee.

First-morning urine samples (n = 240) and venous serum samples (n = 186, owing to parental refusal of venipuncture in some cases) were collected. Hand-wipe samples (n = 240) were collected using isopropanol-soaked gauze wipes from both palms. Indoor dust samples (n = 198) were collected from vacuum cleaner bags or fresh vacuuming of living-room floors. All samples were stored at −20 °C (urine, serum) or −80 °C (dust) until analysis.

 2.2 Questionnaire and PCP use diary

Parents completed a structured questionnaire on sociodemographics, housing characteristics, and frequency of children's PCP use (lotions, sunscreens, hair products, wet wipes). A 7-day diary recorded daily product application events. Product-use frequency was converted into a semi-quantitative score (0–4) for analysis.

 2.3 Analytical methods

Methylsiloxanes (D4, D5, D6, L5, L6, L7) were analyzed by headspace solid-phase microextraction coupled with gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (HS-SPME-GC-MS), following previously validated protocols with modification. Briefly, 1 mL of urine or 0.5 mL of serum was spiked with isotopically labeled internal standards (¹³C₄-D4, ¹³C₅-D5), equilibrated at 40 °C for 20 min, and extracted with a 100 μm polydimethylsiloxane fiber for 30 min. Dust (50 mg) and hand-wipe extracts were sonicated in hexane:acetone (1:1) and cleaned on silica SPE cartridges. Quantification was performed in selected ion monitoring mode. Limits of quantification (LOQ) were 0.05–0.20 ng/mL for urine and serum, 0.02 μg/m² for hand wipes, and 0.05 μg/g for dust. Recovery ranged from 82% to 108%, and relative standard deviations were <12%.

Urinary creatinine was measured by the Jaffé method, and siloxane concentrations were creatinine-corrected for regression analyses.

 2.4 Exposure and risk estimation

Estimated daily intakes (EDI; μg/kg-bw/day) via non-dietary routes were calculated as:

EDI = (C × IR × EF × ED) / (BW × AT)

where C is the concentration in the relevant medium (hand wipe or dust), IR is the ingestion or dermal contact rate, EF is exposure frequency, ED is exposure duration, BW is body weight, and AT is averaging time. Child-specific parameters (hand-to-mouth rate = 0.8–3.2 events/h; dust ingestion = 60–200 mg/day; exposed skin area = 1,600–2,600 cm²) were drawn from published child exposure factors. Dermal absorption fractions of 0.05–0.15 were applied for cVMS.

Hazard quotients (HQ) were calculated as HQ = EDI / TDI, where TDI values were 5 μg/kg-bw/day (D4) and 10 μg/kg-bw/day (D5), consistent with provisional values used in prior assessments. Monte Carlo simulation (10,000 iterations) was used to characterize variability and uncertainty.

 2.5 Quality assurance and statistics

Field blanks, procedural blanks, and duplicate samples (10%) were analyzed with each batch. Blank concentrations were below LOQ for all analytes. Values below LOQ were substituted with LOQ/√2. Data were analyzed using SPSS 26.0, with non-parametric tests for skewed variables, Spearman correlation, and multiple linear regression with log-transformed concentrations. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05.

 3. Results

 3.1 Urinary and serum concentrations

Methylsiloxanes were detected in 91.7% of urine and 78.5% of serum samples. Urinary Σmethylsiloxane concentrations ranged from 12.4 to 486 ng/mL (GM = 74.6 ng/mL; median = 81.2 ng/mL). D5 was the most abundant compound (GM = 31.8 ng/mL), followed by D4 (GM = 19.4 ng/mL) and D6 (GM = 9.7 ng/mL). Linear siloxanes were less frequently detected (L5: 42%; L6: 28%; L7: 11%), with GMs of 2.1–4.6 ng/mL. After creatinine correction, urinary Σmethylsiloxane levels were 96.8 ± 61.3 μg/g creatinine.

Serum concentrations were approximately threefold lower than urine (Σ GM = 21.3 ng/mL; range 3.1–142 ng/mL), with D5 (GM = 9.8 ng/mL) and D4 (GM = 6.2 ng/mL) predominating. Urinary and serum Σmethylsiloxane concentrations were positively correlated (r = 0.61, p < 0.01), supporting the use of urine as a non-invasive biomarker.

 3.2 Age, sex, and regional differences

Urinary Σmethylsiloxane levels were significantly higher in children aged 3–6 years (GM = 96.4 ng/mL) than in those aged 7–12 years (GM = 58.1 ng/mL; p < 0.001). Boys had slightly higher concentrations than girls (GM = 82.3 vs. 66.9 ng/mL; p = 0.048), potentially reflecting greater activity and dust contact. Region A children exhibited higher urinary levels than Region B children (GM = 88.7 vs. 61.5 ng/mL; p = 0.003), consistent with higher reported PCP use in Region A.

 3.3 Non-dietary exposure sources

Hand-wipe siloxane loads ranged from 0.42 to 28.6 μg/m² (GM = 3.82 μg/m²), and indoor dust concentrations ranged from 1.9 to 128 μg/g (GM = 18.7 μg/g). Both were significantly correlated with urinary Σmethylsiloxanes (hand wipe: r = 0.54, p < 0.001; dust: r = 0.38, p < 0.001). Children with PCP use scores in the highest quartile had urinary concentrations 2.4-fold higher than those in the lowest quartile (GM = 138 vs. 57 ng/mL; p < 0.001).

Multiple linear regression explained 52% of the variance in urinary Σmethylsiloxanes. Significant predictors were: PCP use score (β = 0.42, p < 0.001), hand-wipe load (β = 0.27, p < 0.001), dust concentration (β = 0.15, p = 0.012), age (β = −0.18, p = 0.004), and region (β = 0.13, p = 0.021).

 3.4 Exposure and risk estimates

The EDI of total methylsiloxanes via non-dietary routes ranged from 0.09 to 2.74 μg/kg-bw/day (GM = 0.61 μg/kg-bw/day; 95th percentile = 2.11 μg/kg-bw/day). Dermal contact with PCPs accounted for 58–72% of total EDI, hand-to-mouth transfer of hand residues for 18–27%, and dust ingestion for 8–15%. HQs for D4 and D5 were below 1 for the GM and 95th percentile of the general population; however, the HQ for D5 at the 95th percentile reached 0.68, and 4.6% of children exceeded HQ = 1 for combined cVMS.

 4. Discussion

This study provides among the first paired biomarker and non-dietary exposure data for methylsiloxanes in children. The detection frequencies and concentration ranges observed here (urinary Σ GM = 74.6 ng/mL) are comparable to or slightly higher than those reported in adult cohorts and in a small Chinese child pilot study, suggesting ubiquitous and potentially higher exposure in young children. The predominance of D5 and D4 in both urine and serum mirrors their dominance in PCPs and indoor environments.

The strong association between PCP use score and urinary siloxanes confirms that dermal application is the dominant non-dietary pathway in children, consistent with their frequent use of lotions and sunscreens and their high skin surface-area-to-body-weight ratio. The significant contribution of hand-wipe loads and dust indicates that hand-to-mouth behavior and indoor contamination constitute important secondary pathways. The inverse association with age is plausibly explained by more frequent hand-to-mouth activity and greater PCP application per unit body weight in younger children.

The risk characterization suggests that typical exposure is below provisional thresholds, but the narrow margin for D5 at the upper percentiles is noteworthy. Because TDI values remain provisional and do not account for cumulative or endocrine-mediated effects, the HQ of 0.68 for D5 at the 95th percentile may understate risk. Children in the highest exposure stratum—frequent PCP users in homes with elevated dust loads—warrant particular attention.

Several limitations should be acknowledged. First, the cross-sectional design precludes causal inference. Second, urine and serum were collected at a single time point, and the short half-lives of cVMS may lead to exposure misclassification. Third, dermal absorption fractions and ingestion rates carry uncertainty, although Monte Carlo simulation partially addresses this. Fourth, the sample was urban and may not represent rural children. Finally, parent-reported PCP use may be subject to recall bias.

Despite these limitations, the study's strengths include paired multi-matrix sampling, child-specific exposure parameters, and a large sample size relative to prior children's biomonitoring studies. Future work should include longitudinal sampling, metabolite-specific biomarkers, and evaluation of endocrine endpoints.

 5. Conclusion

Children in this study showed widespread internal exposure to methylsiloxanes, with urinary and serum biomarkers reflecting both PCP-derived dermal contact and indoor dust/hand-to-mouth pathways. Although average non-dietary intakes remained below provisional reference values, upper-percentile D5 exposure approached the threshold of concern, indicating a narrow margin of safety for highly exposed children. These findings support the need for child-specific exposure factors in regulatory risk assessment, reduced siloxane content in children's PCPs, and continued biomonitoring to track temporal trends.

title: Discovery of Novel Piperidinylthiazole Derivatives As Broad-Spectrum Fungicidal Candidates
text: The escalating resistance of phytopathogenic fungi to existing agrochemicals, coupled with growing regulatory restrictions on conventional fungicides, necessitates the development of novel antifungal scaffolds with broad-spectrum activity. Herein, a series of novel piperidinylthiazole derivatives was rationally designed, synthesized, and evaluated for fungicidal activity. Systematic structural optimization led to the identification of compound X-12, which exhibited potent in vitro inhibition against a panel of devastating phytopathogens, including *Rhizoctonia solani*, *Botrytis cinerea*, *Fusarium graminearum*, and *Sclerotinia sclerotiorum*, with EC₅₀ values ranging from 0.8 to 6.3 μg/mL, surpassing or comparable to commercial standards. In vivo greenhouse trials further confirmed its protective and curative efficacy against rice sheath blight and cucumber gray mold. Preliminary mechanistic studies suggested that X-12 disrupts fungal cell membrane integrity and interferes with ergosterol biosynthesis. Moreover, the compound displayed favorable crop safety and a low predicted risk to non-target organisms. These findings establish piperidinylthiazole as a promising privileged scaffold for developing next-generation broad-spectrum fungicidal candidates.

title: A 20-year retrospective review of global aquaculture
text:
A 20-year retrospective review of global aquaculture

Abstract

Global aquaculture has undergone transformative expansion over the past two decades, emerging as the fastest-growing food production sector worldwide. This retrospective review synthesises production trends, species composition, regional shifts, and sustainability indicators from 2004 to 2024. Using a harmonised dataset compiled from national statistics, FAO records, and peer-reviewed literature, we estimate that total aquaculture production rose from 45.6 million tonnes in 2004 to 130.2 million tonnes in 2024, representing a compound annual growth rate of 5.4%. Finfish accounted for 52.3% of 2024 output, followed by molluscs (24.1%), crustaceans (17.8%), and aquatic plants (5.8%). Asia remained dominant, contributing 87.4% of global volume, though Africa and Latin America exhibited the highest relative growth rates. Despite these gains, the sector faces persistent challenges, including disease outbreaks, feed dependency, habitat degradation, and climate vulnerability. This review argues that future growth must transition from volume-driven expansion to resilience-oriented intensification, supported by genomic selection, circular feed systems, and integrated multi-trophic aquaculture.

Keywords: aquaculture; production trends; sustainability; blue food; regional development; aquatic species

1. Introduction

The first two decades of the twenty-first century witnessed a profound reconfiguration of global food systems. Capture fisheries, long the primary source of aquatic protein, plateaued at approximately 90–95 million tonnes annually, while aquaculture accelerated rapidly to fill the growing demand for seafood. By 2022, aquaculture had surpassed capture fisheries as the leading source of aquatic animal production destined for human consumption. This transition carries substantial implications for food security, rural livelihoods, trade balances, and ecosystem integrity.

The period from 2004 to 2024 is particularly instructive because it encompasses several distinct phases: a boom in shrimp and salmon production, the rapid rise of tilapia and pangasius in international markets, the expansion of seaweed cultivation for industrial and biofuel applications, and the emergence of offshore and recirculating systems in high-income economies. Simultaneously, the sector encountered structural shocks, including the 2008–2009 financial crisis, the COVID-19 pandemic, and increasingly frequent climate-driven disruptions such as harmful algal blooms and typhoon damage.

Existing reviews have often focused on single species groups, specific regions, or narrow sustainability metrics. A comprehensive twenty-year retrospective that integrates production, species, geography, and sustainability dimensions remains scarce. This paper addresses that gap by asking three questions: (1) How did global aquaculture production and composition change between 2004 and 2024? (2) Which regions and species drove growth or stagnation? (3) What sustainability challenges and innovations emerged, and how might they shape the next two decades?

2. Materials and Methods

This review employed a mixed-method approach combining quantitative synthesis and qualitative assessment. Production data were compiled from the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) FishStatJ database, supplemented by regional aquaculture association reports (e.g., European Aquaculture Society, Asian Fisheries Society) and national statistics from China, India, Indonesia, Vietnam, Norway, Chile, and Egypt. Where discrepancies exceeded 5%, we adopted the median value across sources.

We harmonised species into six functional groups: freshwater finfish, diadromous finfish, marine finfish, crustaceans, molluscs, and aquatic plants. Production volumes were standardised to live weight equivalent. Growth rates were calculated as compound annual growth rates (CAGR) over five-year intervals: 2004–2009, 2009–2014, 2014–2019, and 2019–2024.

Sustainability indicators were derived from peer-reviewed literature published between 2005 and 2024, retrieved via Web of Science and Scopus using combinations of keywords including “aquaculture AND sustainability”, “environmental impact AND fish farming”, and “disease AND aquaculture economics”. A total of 214 articles met inclusion criteria. Qualitative thematic analysis identified recurrent challenges and emerging solutions.

Limitations include reliance on self-reported national data, underreporting of small-scale and subsistence aquaculture, and uneven coverage of environmental performance metrics across regions. These caveats are addressed in the discussion.

3. Results and Analysis

3.1 Production volume and growth

Global aquaculture production increased from 45.6 million tonnes in 2004 to 130.2 million tonnes in 2024. The highest absolute growth occurred between 2009 and 2014 (CAGR 6.1%), followed by a slight deceleration in 2014–2019 (5.3%) and 2019–2024 (4.7%). The slowdown reflects market saturation in established species, stricter environmental regulations, and pandemic-related disruptions in 2020–2021.

3.2 Species composition

Freshwater finfish remained the largest category, rising from 22.1 million tonnes in 2004 to 68.1 million tonnes in 2024. Tilapia and pangasius alone contributed 18.4 million tonnes by 2024. Marine finfish, dominated by Atlantic salmon, grew from 3.2 to 9.7 million tonnes. Crustacean production, led by whiteleg shrimp and black tiger shrimp, expanded from 4.8 to 23.2 million tonnes. Molluscs, primarily oysters, mussels, and scallops, increased from 12.1 to 31.4 million tonnes. Aquatic plants, mainly kelp and Gracilaria, rose from 3.4 to 7.6 million tonnes.

3.3 Regional shifts

Asia’s share of global production declined marginally from 89.8% in 2004 to 87.4% in 2024, but its absolute volume more than doubled. China alone produced 71.3 million tonnes in 2024, though its growth rate slowed to 2.9% annually after 2019 due to environmental restrictions. Southeast Asia emerged as a dynamic hub, with Vietnam, Indonesia, and Bangladesh collectively increasing output by 312% over twenty years. Africa recorded the highest regional CAGR (8.9%), albeit from a low base, reaching 4.1 million tonnes in 2024. Latin America grew at 7.2% annually, driven by Chile’s salmon and Brazil’s tilapia. Europe and North America showed modest growth (2.1% and 1.8%, respectively), constrained by stringent licensing and consumer preferences for wild-caught species.

3.4 Sustainability indicators

Disease outbreaks caused estimated annual losses of 8–12% of production value, with acute hepatopancreatic necrosis disease in shrimp and infectious salmon anaemia in salmon being particularly costly. Feed conversion ratios improved for salmon (from 1.4 to 1.1) and shrimp (from 1.8 to 1.5), but reliance on wild-caught fishmeal and fish oil persisted, with aquaculture consuming 68% of global fishmeal supply in 2024.
