title: Characterization of the interaction between superoxide dismutase and 2-oxoisovalerate dehydrogenase
text: Superoxide dismutase (SOD) and 2-oxoisovalerate dehydrogenase (OIVDH) are key enzymes involved in cellular redox homeostasis and branched-chain amino acid metabolism, respectively. Although both enzymes are localized predominantly in mitochondria and functionally linked to oxidative metabolism, whether they physically interact remains unknown. In this study, we characterized the interaction between SOD and OIVDH using a combination of biochemical and biophysical approaches. Co-immunoprecipitation and pull-down assays demonstrated a direct, specific interaction between the two enzymes in mitochondrial lysates. Surface plasmon resonance analysis revealed a dissociation constant (Kd) in the low micromolar range, indicating a moderate-affinity binding. Molecular docking and site-directed mutagenesis further identified a conserved surface patch on SOD, distinct from its catalytic active site, as the primary binding interface. Notably, binding of OIVDH did not significantly alter the catalytic activity of SOD, but modestly enhanced OIVDH activity in a dose-dependent manner, suggesting a potential regulatory role. Furthermore, the interaction was sensitive to oxidative conditions, with increased binding observed under H₂O₂-induced oxidative stress. Collectively, these findings provide the first evidence for a direct interaction between SOD and OIVDH, implicating a functional coupling between antioxidant defense and branched-chain α-keto acid dehydrogenase activity. This interaction may contribute to the coordination of mitochondrial redox balance and energy metabolism, with potential implications for metabolic disorders associated with oxidative stress.

title: Dominance of Fossil Fuels in Japan's National Energy Mix and Implications for Environmental Sustainability
text:
Dominance of Fossil Fuels in Japan's National Energy Mix and Implications for Environmental Sustainability

Abstract

Japan's energy landscape has long been characterized by a heavy reliance on fossil fuels, a condition exacerbated by the 2011 Fukushima nuclear disaster and the subsequent nationwide shutdown of nuclear reactors. This paper investigates the extent to which fossil fuels dominate Japan's national energy mix and assesses the environmental sustainability implications of this dependency. Using a mixed-methods approach combining quantitative energy data analysis (2010–2023) and qualitative policy review, the study finds that fossil fuels accounted for approximately 72.4% of Japan's primary energy supply in 2023, with coal and liquefied natural gas (LNG) comprising the largest shares. Consequently, Japan's energy-related CO₂ emissions remain among the highest per capita in the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), and the country's Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) targets appear increasingly difficult to achieve. The paper argues that without accelerated deployment of renewables, green hydrogen, and a carefully managed nuclear restart, Japan's fossil fuel lock-in will continue to undermine environmental sustainability and energy security. Policy recommendations are offered, including carbon pricing reform, grid modernization, and regional energy cooperation.

Keywords: Japan; fossil fuels; energy mix; CO₂ emissions; environmental sustainability; energy policy; renewable energy; nuclear power

1. Introduction

Japan is the world's fifth-largest energy consumer and one of the largest importers of fossil fuels. Lacking significant domestic hydrocarbon reserves, the country depends overwhelmingly on imported oil, coal, and liquefied natural gas (LNG) to power its industrial economy, transport sector, and residential heating and cooling. Before the 2011 Great East Japan Earthquake and the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear accident, nuclear power supplied roughly 30% of Japan's electricity, and the government's 2010 Strategic Energy Plan envisaged raising this share to 50% by 2030. The Fukushima disaster reversed this trajectory: by 2013, all nuclear reactors were offline, and fossil fuel-fired generation surged to compensate for the shortfall (METI, 2015; IEA, 2021).

More than a decade later, Japan's energy mix remains structurally carbon-intensive. According to the Institute of Energy Economics, Japan (IEEJ, 2024), fossil fuels accounted for 72.4% of primary energy supply in fiscal year 2023, compared with 6.8% for nuclear, 11.2% for renewables (including hydropower), and 9.6% for other sources. This dependency has profound implications for environmental sustainability. Japan's greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions stood at approximately 1.12 billion metric tons of CO₂-equivalent in FY2022, of which the energy sector contributed over 85% (MOE, 2024). The country has committed under the Paris Agreement to reduce emissions by 46% from 2013 levels by 2030 and to achieve carbon neutrality by 2050. Yet the continued dominance of coal and LNG raises serious questions about the feasibility of these targets.

This paper addresses three research questions: (1) To what extent do fossil fuels dominate Japan's national energy mix? (2) What are the environmental sustainability consequences of this dominance? (3) What policy measures could facilitate a transition toward a more sustainable energy system? The study contributes to the broader literature on energy transitions in resource-poor, industrialized economies and offers policy-relevant insights for Japan and comparable countries.

2. Materials and Methods

This study employs a mixed-methods design integrating quantitative analysis of secondary energy data with qualitative policy document review.

Quantitative data were drawn from publicly available databases, including the International Energy Agency (IEA) World Energy Balances, the Energy Information Administration (EIA) International Energy Statistics, Japan's Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI) Agency for Natural Resources and Energy, and the Ministry of the Environment (MOE). The dataset covers the period 2010–2023, encompassing the pre- and post-Fukushima eras. Key variables include primary energy supply by source (oil, coal, natural gas/LNG, nuclear, hydro, renewables), electricity generation mix, energy-related CO₂ emissions, and energy intensity (TPES/GDP).

Data analysis proceeded in three steps. First, descriptive statistics and trend analysis were used to characterize the evolution of Japan's energy mix, with compound annual growth rates (CAGR) calculated for each energy source. Second, a decomposition analysis based on the Kaya identity was applied to identify the relative contributions of population, affluence, energy intensity, and carbon intensity to changes in CO₂ emissions. Third, a comparative benchmarking exercise positioned Japan against selected OECD peers (Germany, the United Kingdom, South Korea) to contextualize its decarbonization performance.

Qualitative data comprised Japan's Strategic Energy Plan (2021), the Green Growth Strategy (2020), the Sixth Strategic Energy Plan, and submissions to the UNFCCC, as well as peer-reviewed literature on energy transitions. These documents were coded thematically to identify policy priorities, barriers, and stated targets.

Limitations include reliance on self-reported national data and the absence of primary fieldwork. Nevertheless, triangulation across multiple authoritative sources enhances the reliability of the findings.

3. Results and Analysis

3.1 Fossil Fuel Dominance

The data reveal a persistent and substantial fossil fuel share in Japan's primary energy supply. In FY2010, fossil fuels accounted for 81.2% of total primary energy supply; by FY2023, this figure had declined only modestly to 72.4%. Oil remained the single largest source at 34.1%, followed by coal at 22.8% and natural gas/LNG at 15.5%. The modest decline reflects the gradual restart of nuclear reactors (10 units as of 2024) and the expansion of solar photovoltaic (PV) capacity, which grew from 3.6 GW in 2011 to approximately 87 GW in 2023 (IEA, 2024).

In the electricity sector, fossil fuels generated 68.9% of electricity in FY2023, with LNG contributing 32.4%, coal 30.1%, and oil 6.4%. Nuclear provided 8.5%, hydropower 7.6%, and other renewables (solar, wind, biomass) 15.0%. Although renewable electricity generation has more than doubled since 2015, its growth has been outpaced by the persistence of coal and LNG, both of which benefit from long-term contracts and existing infrastructure.

3.2 Environmental Implications

Japan's energy-related CO₂ emissions declined from 1.24 billion tons in FY2010 to 1.05 billion tons in FY2022, a reduction of 15.3%. However, decomposition analysis indicates that most of this decline stemmed from reduced economic activity and improved energy efficiency rather than fuel switching. The carbon intensity of Japan's energy supply (CO₂ per unit of TPES) remained at 2.31 tCO₂/toe in 2022, significantly higher than the OECD average of 1.98 tCO₂/toe and far above France (0.89) and the United Kingdom (1.42).

Per capita CO₂ emissions stood at 8.5 tons in 2022, compared with 7.7 tons for Germany and 7.1 tons for the UK. Japan's emissions reduction trajectory is thus insufficient to meet its 2030 NDC target of a 46% reduction from 2013 levels; current policies are projected to deliver only a 30–35% reduction (IEEJ, 2024). The continued combustion of coal—the most carbon-intensive fossil fuel—is particularly problematic, as Japan remains the only G7 country still constructing new coal-fired power plants (three units under construction as of 2024).

Beyond climate change, fossil fuel dependence entails air pollution and health externalities. Although Japan's air quality is relatively good by international standards, NOx and PM2.5 emissions from coal and oil combustion contribute to respiratory illness, particularly in urban-industrial corridors. The environmental sustainability implications are therefore both global (climate) and local (air quality, ecosystem acidification).

3.3 Comparative Benchmarking

Compared with Germany and the UK, Japan has decarbonized its power sector more slowly. Germany reduced coal's share of electricity from 43% in 2010 to 26% in 2023, while the UK cut coal from 28% to zero over the same period. Japan's coal share fell only from 25% to 30% (in fact rising after Fukushima before declining slightly). The UK's success stemmed from carbon pricing (the Carbon Price Support), renewable auctions, and grid interconnection; Japan lacks a comparable carbon price and faces geographical constraints on cross-border grid integration.

4. Discussion

The findings confirm that fossil fuels continue to dominate Japan's energy mix, with only modest structural change since 2010. Several factors explain this persistence. First, the Fukushima disaster created a political and regulatory vacuum that slowed nuclear restarts and discouraged new investment. Second, Japan's geography limits the potential for cross-border electricity trade and large-scale hydropower, making variable renewables harder to integrate without costly storage and grid upgrades. Third, powerful incumbent interests—utilities, trading houses, and the coal and LNG supply chain—have resisted rapid change. Fourth, Japan's industrial policy has prioritized energy security and affordability over decarbonization, leading to the continued use of coal and LNG as "bridge" fuels.

The environmental implications are serious. Japan's current trajectory is incompatible with the Paris Agreement's 1.5°C goal. The continued construction of coal plants creates carbon lock-in and stranded asset risks. Moreover, reliance on LNG—often promoted as a transition fuel—may delay the deployment of truly zero-carbon alternatives, as LNG infrastructure has a 30–40 year operational lifespan.

Nevertheless, there are signs of change. The Sixth Strategic Energy Plan (2021) targets 36–38% renewable electricity by 2030 and 20–22% nuclear. Japan has launched its Green Transformation (GX) strategy, including a carbon pricing mechanism (GX League) and green hydrogen and ammonia co-firing pilots. However, these measures remain incremental. A more ambitious approach would require: (1) a robust carbon tax or emissions trading system covering the power sector; (2) accelerated deployment of offshore wind (Japan has vast potential but only 0.5 GW installed as of 2024); (3) reform of the electricity market to prioritize renewables; (4) regional cooperation on hydrogen and ammonia supply chains; and (5) a transparent, safety-first nuclear restart program.

The study's limitations include its reliance on aggregate national data, which may mask regional disparities, and the hypothetical nature of some projections. Future research should examine subnational energy transitions and the role of municipal climate policies.

5. Conclusion

This paper has demonstrated that fossil fuels remain overwhelmingly dominant in Japan's national energy mix, accounting for 72.4% of primary energy supply and 68.9% of electricity generation in FY2023. This dominance has significant environmental sustainability implications: Japan's CO₂ emissions remain high by OECD standards, its 2030 NDC target is unlikely to be met under current policies, and continued coal and LNG use creates carbon lock-in and health externalities. The persistence of fossil fuels is rooted in the post-Fukushima nuclear shutdown, geographical constraints, incumbent interests, and a policy emphasis on energy security over decarbonization.

Achieving environmental sustainability will require a fundamental reorientation of Japan's energy policy. Priority measures include carbon pricing, massive investment in offshore wind and grid infrastructure, a managed nuclear restart, and regional cooperation on green hydrogen. Without such measures, Japan risks falling further behind its G7 peers and undermining global climate goals. The case of Japan illustrates a broader lesson for resource-poor industrialized economies: energy security and environmental sustainability are not mutually exclusive, but reconciling them demands political will and structural reform.

title: View of Pakistani Residents toward Coronavirus Disease (COVID-19) during a Rapid Outbreak: A Rapid Online Survey
text: The COVID-19 pandemic, caused by SARS-CoV-2, has spread rapidly across the globe since its emergence in late 2019. Pakistan reported its first confirmed case in February 2020, followed by a sharp increase in infections and subsequent public health measures. Pakistan’s residents, like many populations in low- and middle-income countries, face unique socio-economic, cultural, and healthcare challenges that may shape their response to the outbreak. Understanding public knowledge, attitudes, and practices toward COVID-19 is critical for designing effective risk communication and containment strategies. However, data on Pakistani residents’ views during the early phase of the rapid outbreak remain limited. Therefore, this study conducted a rapid online survey to assess the knowledge, perceptions, and preventive behaviors of Pakistani residents regarding COVID-19, aiming to identify gaps and inform targeted public health interventions.

title: Religiosity and Beliefs About the Transmission of Cancer, Chemotherapy, and Radiation Through Physical Contact in Saudi Arabia
text:
Results and Discussion

A total of 412 participants completed the survey (response rate 82.4%). Mean age was 34.6 years (SD = 9.8); 58.5% were female, and 71.1% reported praying at least daily. Overall, 46.6% endorsed at least one misconception about cancer transmission through physical contact, 38.3% believed chemotherapy could be transmitted by touch, and 31.8% believed the same of radiation. Misconceptions were significantly more prevalent among participants with lower education (58.9% vs. 33.2%; χ² = 24.7, p < .001) and among those attributing illness to divine punishment (OR = 2.14, 95% CI [1.38, 3.32]). Higher intrinsic religiosity scores correlated positively with transmission beliefs (r = .29, p < .01), whereas frequency of mosque attendance showed no association (r = .06, p = .21).

These findings suggest that misconceptions about cancer transmission are common in Saudi Arabia and are linked less to religious practice per se than to specific theological attributions and limited health literacy. The positive association with intrinsic religiosity may reflect fatalistic appraisals of illness rather than doctrine itself, consistent with studies linking fatalism to stigma in other Muslim-majority populations (e.g., Egypt, Malaysia). The absence of an attendance effect supports this interpretation: communal worship does not appear to propagate these beliefs. Clinically, the results argue for culturally tailored education that engages religious leaders as trusted messengers, explicitly distinguishing spiritual contagion concepts from biomedical transmission. Limitations include convenience sampling, self-report bias, and a cross-sectional design that precludes causal inference. Future work should test mosque-based educational interventions to reduce stigma toward cancer patients and survivors.

title: A Machine Learning Model for Accurate Prediction of Sepsis in ICU Patients
text:
A Machine Learning Model for Accurate Prediction of Sepsis in ICU Patients

Abstract

Sepsis remains a leading cause of mortality in intensive care units (ICUs), where delayed recognition substantially increases the risk of irreversible organ dysfunction and death. This study develops and evaluates a machine learning model for the early and accurate prediction of sepsis using routinely collected ICU data. A retrospective dataset of 4,872 ICU admissions was constructed, containing demographic variables, vital signs, laboratory results, and clinical scores recorded within the first 24 hours of admission. After preprocessing and feature selection, six algorithms—logistic regression, random forest, gradient boosting, support vector machine, extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), and a multilayer perceptron—were trained and compared. The XGBoost model achieved the best performance, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.913, sensitivity of 0.861, specificity of 0.874, and F1-score of 0.842 in the held-out test set. SHAP analysis identified lactate, sequential organ failure assessment (SOFA) score, heart rate, temperature, and white blood cell count as the most influential predictors. The results suggest that machine learning can support clinicians in identifying sepsis earlier than conventional scoring systems, although prospective validation and workflow integration remain necessary before routine deployment.

Keywords: sepsis; intensive care unit; machine learning; early prediction; XGBoost; clinical decision support

1. Introduction

Sepsis is defined as life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by a dysregulated host response to infection. It affects millions of patients worldwide each year and accounts for a substantial proportion of ICU mortality. The Surviving Sepsis Campaign emphasizes that early recognition and timely administration of antibiotics and fluids are critical to improving outcomes. However, early diagnosis remains challenging because initial presentations are often nonspecific, and conventional scoring systems such as the Systemic Inflammatory Response Syndrome criteria and the SOFA score have limited discriminative ability in heterogeneous ICU populations.

In recent years, machine learning has emerged as a promising approach for sepsis prediction. Unlike rule-based scoring systems, machine learning models can capture complex, nonlinear interactions among numerous clinical variables and can be updated as new data become available. Several studies have reported encouraging results using electronic health record data, but many models suffer from class imbalance, missing values, and limited generalizability. Moreover, the “black-box” nature of some algorithms raises concerns regarding clinical trust and interpretability.

This study aims to develop a machine learning model for accurate sepsis prediction in ICU patients using data available within the first 24 hours of admission. The specific objectives are: (1) to compare multiple machine learning algorithms under a unified preprocessing pipeline; (2) to evaluate predictive performance using AUROC, sensitivity, specificity, and F1-score; and (3) to interpret the best-performing model using feature importance analysis. We hypothesize that a gradient boosting-based model can outperform traditional logistic regression and provide clinically meaningful predictors.

2. Materials and Methods

2.1 Data Source and Study Population

We conducted a retrospective analysis using a de-identified ICU database containing 4,872 adult admissions from a tertiary care center between January 2018 and December 2022. Inclusion criteria were: age ≥18 years, ICU length of stay ≥24 hours, and availability of at least one set of vital signs and laboratory results within the first 24 hours. Patients with sepsis present on admission, defined by a SOFA increase of ≥2 points before ICU admission, were excluded to focus on early prediction rather than prevalent cases. The final cohort included 3,914 patients, of whom 612 (15.6%) developed sepsis during the ICU stay according to the Sepsis-3 criteria.

2.2 Variables and Outcome

A total of 42 candidate predictors were extracted, including demographic characteristics (age, sex), vital signs (heart rate, systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure, respiratory rate, temperature, oxygen saturation), laboratory values (white blood cell count, platelet count, creatinine, bilirubin, lactate, C-reactive protein, procalcitonin), and clinical scores (SOFA, APACHE II). The primary outcome was the occurrence of sepsis within 72 hours after ICU admission. For patients who developed sepsis, data from the 24-hour window preceding diagnosis were used; for non-sepsis patients, data from the first 24 hours were used.

2.3 Data Preprocessing

Missing values were imputed using multiple imputation by chained equations, with the number of imputations set to five. Continuous variables were standardized to zero mean and unit variance. Categorical variables were one-hot encoded. To address class imbalance, synthetic minority oversampling technique (SMOTE) was applied to the training set only, avoiding data leakage into the test set. The dataset was randomly split into a training set (70%, n=2,740), a validation set (15%, n=587), and a test set (15%, n=587), stratified by outcome.

2.4 Model Development and Evaluation

Six algorithms were trained: logistic regression with L2 regularization, random forest, gradient boosting, support vector machine with radial basis function kernel, XGBoost, and a multilayer perceptron with two hidden layers. Hyperparameters were tuned using five-fold cross-validation on the training set and evaluated on the validation set. The best configuration for each algorithm was then applied to the test set.

Performance metrics included AUROC, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, negative predictive value, and F1-score. The optimal threshold was determined by maximizing the Youden index on the validation set. Calibration was assessed using the Brier score and calibration curves. For interpretability, SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) values were computed for the best model.

3. Results and Analysis

3.1 Baseline Characteristics

The mean age of the cohort was 63.4 ± 15.2 years, and 54.1% were male. Patients who developed sepsis had higher baseline SOFA scores (6.8 ± 2.4 vs. 3.1 ± 1.9, p < 0.001), higher lactate levels (3.2 ± 1.8 vs. 1.6 ± 0.9 mmol/L, p < 0.001), and higher heart rates (108 ± 22 vs. 89 ± 18 bpm, p < 0.001) compared with non-sepsis patients. The median time from ICU admission to sepsis onset was 28 hours (interquartile range, 14–46 hours).

3.2 Model Performance

Table 1 summarizes the test set performance of all models. XGBoost achieved the highest AUROC (0.913, 95% CI: 0.892–0.934), followed by gradient boosting (0.901), random forest (0.887), multilayer perceptron (0.879), support vector machine (0.862), and logistic regression (0.834). At the optimal threshold, XGBoost yielded sensitivity of 0.861, specificity of 0.874, positive predictive value of 0.823, negative predictive value of 0.902, and F1-score of 0.842. The Brier score was 0.112, indicating good calibration.

3.3 Feature Importance

SHAP analysis revealed that the five most influential features for XGBoost were lactate (mean |SHAP| = 0.41), SOFA score (0.37), heart rate (0.29), temperature (0.24), and white blood cell count (0.22). Lower systolic blood pressure and higher respiratory rate also contributed substantially. The direction of effects was clinically plausible: higher lactate, higher SOFA, tachycardia, fever or hypothermia, and leukocytosis increased the predicted probability of sepsis.

3.4 Subgroup Analysis

The model performed consistently across age groups (<65 vs. ≥65 years), sex, and admission type (medical vs. surgical). AUROC ranged from 0.891 to 0.924, with no significant difference between subgroups (p > 0.05). Performance was slightly lower in patients with chronic kidney disease (AUROC 0.884), possibly due to altered lactate metabolism.

4. Discussion

This study demonstrates that a machine learning model based on routinely available ICU data can predict sepsis with high accuracy. The XGBoost model outperformed logistic regression and other algorithms, consistent with previous reports that gradient boosting methods effectively capture nonlinear relationships in clinical data. The AUROC of 0.913 is comparable to or higher than those reported in several prior studies, although direct comparison is limited by differences in cohort definition, prediction window, and outcome ascertainment.

The SHAP results enhance clinical interpretability. Lactate and SOFA score emerged as the strongest predictors, which aligns with their established roles in sepsis diagnosis and prognosis. Heart rate and temperature reflect the systemic inflammatory response, while white blood cell count indicates immune activation. These findings suggest that the model’s decisions are not arbitrary but are grounded in well-recognized pathophysiological mechanisms.

Despite these strengths, several limitations should be acknowledged. First, the retrospective, single-center design may limit generalizability. Second, although multiple imputation and SMOTE were used, residual bias from missing data and synthetic samples cannot be excluded. Third, the prediction window was limited to 72 hours; longer-term prediction may require temporal modeling approaches such as recurrent neural networks. Fourth, the model was not prospectively validated, and its impact on clinical outcomes remains unknown. Future work should include external validation, prospective silent trials, and integration into electronic health record systems with real-time alerts.

5. Conclusion

In conclusion, an XGBoost-based machine learning model using routine ICU data achieved accurate early prediction of sepsis, with AUROC of 0.913 and balanced sensitivity and specificity. Key predictors included lactate, SOFA score, heart rate, temperature, and white blood cell count. The model has the potential to support early clinical decision-making, but prospective validation and careful implementation are essential before widespread clinical use.

title: Population genetic analysis of aquaculture salmonid populations in China using a 57K rainbow trout SNP array
text:
Title: Population genetic analysis of aquaculture salmonid populations in China using a 57K rainbow trout SNP array

Abstract
Rainbow trout (*Oncorhynchus mykiss*) is a major aquaculture species in China, yet the genetic background of domestic stocks remains poorly characterized. Here, we genotyped 480 individuals from eight aquaculture populations across four provinces using a 57K rainbow trout SNP array. After quality control, 48,215 SNPs were retained. Mean observed heterozygosity ranged from 0.281 to 0.334, and pairwise F_ST values varied from 0.018 to 0.112. Principal component analysis and ADMIXTURE clustering revealed three genetic clusters, broadly corresponding to northern, central, and southwestern production regions. Linkage disequilibrium decayed rapidly (r² < 0.2 within 40 kb), suggesting large effective population sizes (N_e = 186–412). Runs of homozygosity indicated modest inbreeding (F_ROH = 0.021–0.068). These results provide a baseline for genetic improvement and conservation of rainbow trout germplasm in China.

Keywords: *Oncorhynchus mykiss*; SNP array; population structure; aquaculture genetics; linkage disequilibrium; runs of homozygosity

Introduction
Salmonid aquaculture in China has expanded rapidly, with rainbow trout production exceeding 40,000 tonnes annually. Despite this growth, most broodstock derives from a limited number of imported lineages, raising concerns about inbreeding and reduced adaptive potential. Molecular markers such as microsatellites have been used previously, but genome-wide SNP panels offer higher resolution for estimating diversity, structure, and effective population size. The recent development of a 57K rainbow trout SNP array enables standardized, high-throughput genotyping across hatcheries. This study aimed to (i) quantify genetic diversity within and among eight Chinese aquaculture populations, (ii) infer population structure and admixture, and (iii) estimate linkage disequilibrium and inbreeding levels to inform breeding programs.

Materials and Methods
*Sampling and DNA extraction.* Fin clips were collected from 480 individuals (60 per population) from eight farms: Harbin (HB), Beijing (BJ), Shandong (SD), Henan (HN), Hubei (HU), Sichuan (SC), Yunnan (YN), and Guizhou (GZ). Genomic DNA was extracted using a salt-out method and quantified by spectrophotometry.

*Genotyping and quality control.* Samples were genotyped on a 57K rainbow trout SNP array (Affymetrix Axiom). PLINK v1.9 was used for filtering: individuals with call rate <95% and SNPs with call rate <90%, minor allele frequency <0.01, or Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium deviation (P < 10⁻⁶) were removed. After filtering, 48,215 SNPs and 462 individuals remained.

*Statistical analysis.* Observed (H_O) and expected (H_E) heterozygosities, nucleotide diversity (π), and F_ST were computed in PLINK and VCFtools. PCA was performed in GCTA. ADMIXTURE estimated ancestry coefficients (K = 2–6). Linkage disequilibrium (r²) was calculated for syntenic SNP pairs using PLINK. Effective population size (N_e) was estimated via the linkage disequilibrium method in NeEstimator v2. Runs of homozygosity (ROH) were identified with PLINK (--homozyg), and F_ROH was calculated per individual.

Results
*Genetic diversity.* Mean H_O across populations ranged from 0.281 (YN) to 0.334 (HB), while H_E ranged from 0.302 to 0.347. Nucleotide diversity (π) varied between 0.0021 and 0.0029. The YN and GZ populations showed the lowest diversity, consistent with smaller census sizes.

*Population structure.* Pairwise F_ST ranged from 0.018 (HB vs BJ) to 0.112 (YN vs SD). PCA separated populations along PC1 (18.4% variance) and PC2 (7.1%), with northern populations (HB, BJ, SD) clustering together, central populations (HN, HU) forming an intermediate group, and southwestern populations (SC, YN, GZ) diverging. ADMIXTURE showed lowest cross-validation error at K = 3, confirming three ancestral clusters. Admixture proportions indicated historical introgression between central and northern stocks.

*Linkage disequilibrium and N_e.* Mean r² declined from 0.41 at 1 kb to 0.17 at 40 kb, with a half-decay distance of ~22 kb. N_e estimates ranged from 186 (YN) to 412 (HB), suggesting moderate to large effective sizes despite domestication.

*Inbreeding.* F_ROH ranged from 0.021 (HB) to 0.068 (YN). Short ROH (<2 Mb) dominated, indicating ancient inbreeding; however, YN and GZ harbored longer ROH (>5 Mb), suggesting recent parental relatedness.

Discussion
This study represents the first large-scale SNP-based survey of rainbow trout aquaculture populations in China. The three genetic clusters align with geographic and historical stocking records: northern farms rely on Danish and Norwegian strains, central farms on mixed imports, and southwestern farms on locally adapted lineages. The moderate F_ST values (mean 0.054) indicate substantial differentiation, likely driven by limited gene flow and founder effects.

Heterozygosity levels were comparable to wild North American populations (H_O ≈ 0.30–0.35), but lower than some European hatchery strains. The reduced diversity in YN and GZ populations warrants attention, as low N_e (186–240) increases genetic drift and inbreeding depression risk. ROH patterns confirm that inbreeding is present but not severe; nevertheless, longer ROH in southwestern stocks suggest recent bottlenecks.

Linkage disequilibrium decay was faster than in Atlantic salmon, consistent with the large ancestral N_e of rainbow trout. This rapid decay supports genome-wide association studies with moderate marker density, though imputation may be needed for fine-mapping.

Management implications include: (1) establishing a national germplasm repository to preserve distinct clusters; (2) exchanging broodstock between YN/GZ and HB/BJ to reduce inbreeding; (3) using genomic estimated breeding values (GEBV) to select for growth and disease resistance while controlling coancestry.

Conclusion
The 57K SNP array resolved population structure and diversity in Chinese aquaculture rainbow trout. Three genetic clusters correspond to northern, central, and southwestern regions. While overall diversity is moderate, southwestern populations show reduced N_e and elevated ROH, indicating a need for targeted conservation and controlled crossbreeding. These findings provide a genomic foundation for sustainable salmonid aquaculture in China.

References (omitted for brevity; typical citations would include PLINK, ADMIXTURE, and rainbow trout genome papers.)

title: Research on logistics carbon emissions under the coupling and coordination scenario of logistics industry and financial industry
text: Abstract: The logistics industry is a major contributor to carbon emissions, and its green transformation urgently requires financial support. This paper investigates logistics carbon emissions under the coupling and coordination scenario of the logistics industry and the financial industry. A coupling coordination degree model is constructed to measure the interactive relationship between the two industries, and a scenario analysis framework is developed to simulate logistics carbon emissions under different coupling coordination levels. Using panel data from 30 Chinese provinces, the results show that the coupling coordination degree between the logistics industry and the financial industry exhibits a fluctuating upward trend with significant regional heterogeneity. Scenario simulations indicate that a higher coupling coordination level corresponds to lower logistics carbon emission intensity, and the synergistic effect is most pronounced in eastern regions. Financial agglomeration, technological innovation, and industrial structure upgrading are identified as key mediating channels. These findings provide policy implications for promoting cross-industry coordination to achieve logistics decarbonization.

title: Apple rootstocks with different phosphorus efficiency exhibit alterations in rhizosphere bacterial structure
text:
Apple rootstocks with different phosphorus efficiency exhibit alterations in rhizosphere bacterial structure

Abstract

Phosphorus (P) deficiency is a major constraint for apple production in calcareous soils. Rootstocks play a critical role in mediating plant adaptation to low-P stress, yet the extent to which rootstock P efficiency shapes the rhizosphere bacterial community remains poorly understood. In this study, two apple rootstock genotypes with contrasting P efficiency—the P-efficient *Malus hupehensis* Rehd. and the P-inefficient *Malus domestica* Borkh. ‘M9’—were cultivated in a low-P soil under controlled conditions. Rhizosphere bacterial communities were characterized using 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing, and soil physicochemical properties and plant P status were determined. The P-efficient rootstock exhibited significantly higher biomass, root-to-shoot ratio, acid phosphatase activity, and P accumulation than the P-inefficient rootstock. Rhizosphere bacterial richness (Chao1) and Shannon diversity were significantly greater in the P-efficient genotype. Principal coordinate analysis based on Bray–Curtis distances revealed a clear separation of bacterial communities between the two rootstock genotypes (PERMANOVA, R² = 0.42, P < 0.001). The P-efficient rootstock enriched members of *Proteobacteria*, particularly *Pseudomonas*, *Burkholderia*, and *Rhizobium*, as well as *Bacillus* and *Streptomyces*, whereas the P-inefficient rootstock was dominated by *Acidobacteria* and *Actinobacteria*. Redundancy analysis indicated that rhizosphere pH, available P, and acid phosphatase activity were the principal drivers of community variation, explaining 58.3% of the total variance. Co-occurrence network analysis showed that the P-efficient rhizosphere network was more complex and modular, with more positive interactions. These findings demonstrate that apple rootstocks with contrasting P efficiency recruit distinct rhizosphere bacterial assemblages, likely through root-mediated modifications of the rhizosphere environment, and suggest that harnessing beneficial rhizobacteria may improve P acquisition in apple orchards.

Keywords: apple rootstock; phosphorus efficiency; rhizosphere; bacterial community; 16S rRNA sequencing; acid phosphatase

1. Introduction

Phosphorus (P) is an essential macronutrient for plant growth and development, participating in energy metabolism, nucleic acid synthesis, membrane integrity, and signal transduction. Although total P in soils is often abundant, most of it exists in insoluble forms that are unavailable to plants, particularly in calcareous and acidic soils. Apple (*Malus* spp.) is one of the most economically important fruit crops worldwide, and P deficiency frequently limits tree growth, fruit yield, and quality. Conventional management relies heavily on P fertilizer application; however, P use efficiency in orchards is generally low, and excessive fertilization leads to environmental pollution and soil degradation. Therefore, developing strategies to enhance plant P acquisition is of great agronomic and environmental significance.

Rootstocks are widely used in apple cultivation to control tree vigor, improve fruit quality, and enhance tolerance to biotic and abiotic stresses. Increasing evidence indicates that rootstocks differ substantially in their ability to acquire P from soil, a trait termed P efficiency. P-efficient rootstocks typically exhibit morphological and physiological adaptations, including altered root architecture, increased root hair density, enhanced secretion of protons and organic acids, and elevated activity of acid phosphatases. These root-mediated changes not only mobilize sparingly soluble P but also modify the rhizosphere microenvironment, which in turn influences the composition and function of rhizosphere microorganisms.

The rhizosphere harbors a diverse and dynamic bacterial community that plays a pivotal role in plant nutrient acquisition. Phosphate-solubilizing bacteria (PSB), including members of *Pseudomonas*, *Bacillus*, *Burkholderia*, and *Rhizobium*, can convert insoluble P into plant-available forms through the production of organic acids, phosphatases, and siderophores. In addition, rhizobacteria can promote plant growth via phytohormone production, nitrogen fixation, and biocontrol of pathogens. The composition of the rhizosphere bacterial community is shaped by plant genotype, root exudates, soil properties, and agricultural practices. Accumulating evidence from crops such as wheat, maize, and rice suggests that plant genotypes with superior P efficiency recruit distinct microbial assemblages that facilitate P mobilization. However, whether apple rootstocks with contrasting P efficiency similarly shape rhizosphere bacterial communities remains largely unexplored.

We hypothesized that apple rootstocks differing in P efficiency would (i) differ in rhizosphere soil chemical properties and enzyme activities, and (ii) recruit distinct rhizosphere bacterial communities, with the P-efficient genotype enriching taxa associated with P solubilization and plant growth promotion. To test these hypotheses, we compared the P-efficient *Malus hupehensis* Rehd. and the P-inefficient *M. domestica* ‘M9’ grown in a low-P soil, integrating plant physiological measurements, soil biochemical analyses, and 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing. Our results provide novel insights into the rootstock–microbiome interactions underlying P efficiency in apple and offer a theoretical basis for exploiting beneficial rhizobacteria in sustainable orchard management.

2. Materials and Methods

2.1 Plant materials and experimental design

Two apple rootstock genotypes with contrasting P efficiency were used: *Malus hupehensis* Rehd. (P-efficient) and *Malus domestica* Borkh. ‘M9’ (P-inefficient). The experiment was conducted in a greenhouse at Shandong Agricultural University (36°09′N, 117°09′E) from March to August 2023. Uniform one-year-old seedlings were transplanted into plastic pots (25 cm diameter, 30 cm height) filled with 8 kg of low-P calcareous soil (available P 4.2 mg kg⁻¹, pH 8.1, organic matter 11.3 g kg⁻¹). The soil was collected from the 0–20 cm layer of an apple orchard with a history of P deficiency. The experiment followed a completely randomized design with two treatments (rootstock genotypes) and ten replicates per treatment. Plants were watered regularly to maintain 60–70% of field capacity, and no P fertilizer was applied during the experiment. After 120 days of growth, plants were harvested for analysis.

2.2 Plant growth and P status measurements

At harvest, shoots and roots were separated, and root systems were carefully washed with distilled water. Biomass was determined after oven-drying at 75 °C to constant weight. Root-to-shoot ratio was calculated on a dry weight basis. Total P concentrations in shoots and roots were determined by the molybdenum blue method after digestion with H₂SO₄–H₂O₂. P accumulation was calculated as the product of biomass and P concentration.

2.3 Rhizosphere soil collection and biochemical analyses

Rhizosphere soil was collected by gently shaking the roots, and soil adhering to the root surface (approximately 2 mm) was brushed into sterile tubes, immediately frozen in liquid nitrogen, and stored at −80 °C for DNA extraction. A portion of the soil was air-dried for chemical analysis. Soil pH was measured in a 1:2.5 (w/v) soil–water suspension. Available P was extracted with 0.5 M NaHCO₃ (pH 8.5) and determined by the molybdenum blue method. Acid phosphatase activity was assayed using p-nitrophenyl phosphate as substrate and expressed as μg p-nitrophenol g⁻¹ soil h⁻¹.

2.4 DNA extraction, PCR amplification, and sequencing

Total genomic DNA was extracted from 0.5 g of rhizosphere soil using the FastDNA SPIN Kit for Soil (MP Biomedicals, USA) according to the manufacturer’s instructions. The V3–V4 hypervariable region of the 16S rRNA gene was amplified with primers 338F (5′-ACTCCTACGGGAGGCAGCAG-3′) and 806R (5′-GGACTACHVGGGTWTCTAAT-3′). PCR products were purified, quantified, and sequenced on an Illumina NovaSeq 6000 platform (Novogene, Beijing, China).

2.5 Bioinformatics and statistical analysis

Raw sequences were quality-filtered using QIIME2 (v2022.8). Chimeric sequences were removed with UCHIME, and high-quality sequences were clustered into amplicon sequence variants (ASVs) at 100% similarity using DADA2. Taxonomic assignment was performed against the SILVA 138 database. Alpha diversity indices (Chao1 and Shannon) were calculated using the vegan package in R. Beta diversity was assessed by Bray–Curtis distances and visualized by principal coordinate analysis (PCoA). Permutational multivariate analysis of variance (PERMANOVA) was used to test community differences. Redundancy analysis (RDA) was performed to identify soil factors driving community variation. Co-occurrence networks were constructed based on Spearman correlations (|r| > 0.7, P < 0.01) and visualized in Gephi. Differences between treatments were tested by independent-sample t-tests at P < 0.05.

3. Results and Analysis

3.1 Plant growth and P status

The P-efficient rootstock *M. hupehensis* exhibited significantly greater shoot biomass (5.82 g vs. 3.47 g), root biomass (3.15 g vs. 1.62 g), and total biomass (8.97 g vs. 5.09 g) than the P-inefficient ‘M9’ (P < 0.05). The root-to-shoot ratio was also higher in *M. hupehensis* (0.54 vs. 0.47, P < 0.05). Total P concentration in shoots was 1.86 mg g⁻¹ in *M. hupehensis* compared with 1.21 mg g⁻¹ in ‘M9’, and root P concentration showed a similar trend (1.42 vs. 0.98 mg g⁻¹). Consequently, total P accumulation in *M. hupehensis* was 2.3-fold higher than in ‘M9’ (16.7 mg vs. 7.3 mg per plant, P < 0.01).

3.2 Rhizosphere soil properties and enzyme activity

Rhizosphere pH was significantly lower in *M. hupehensis* (7.62) than in ‘M9’ (7.94) (P < 0.05). Available P in the rhizosphere of *M. hupehensis* was 6.8 mg kg⁻¹, 1.7-fold higher than that of ‘M9’ (4.0 mg kg⁻¹, P < 0.01). Acid phosphatase activity was markedly higher in the P-efficient genotype (28.4 vs. 16.9 μg p-nitrophenol g⁻¹ h⁻¹, P < 0.01).

3.3 Bacterial diversity and community composition

A total of 1,842,376 high-quality sequences were obtained, with an average of 92,119 sequences per sample, clustered into 4,236 ASVs. Chao1 and Shannon indices were significantly higher in the rhizosphere of *M. hupehensis* than in ‘M9’ (Chao1: 2,845 vs. 2,213; Shannon: 6.42 vs. 5.78; P < 0.05). PCoA based on Bray–Curtis distances showed a clear separation between the two rootstock genotypes along the first principal coordinate (PCo1 = 38.6% of variance), and PERMANOVA confirmed a significant genotype effect (R² = 0.42, P < 0.001).

At the phylum level, *Proteobacteria* was the most abundant taxon in both rhizospheres, but its relative abundance was significantly higher in *M. hupehensis* (46.3%) than in ‘M9’ (34.7%) (P < 0.01). In contrast, *Acidobacteria* (18.2% vs. 11.5%) and *Actinobacteria* (15.6% vs. 10.8%) were enriched in ‘M9’ (P < 0.05). At the genus level, the P-efficient rootstock was enriched in *Pseudomonas* (5.8% vs. 2.1%), *Burkholderia* (3.4% vs. 1.2%), *Rhizobium* (2.9% vs. 1.1%), *Bacillus* (2.6% vs. 0.9%), and *Streptomyces* (2.2% vs. 1.3%) (all P < 0.05). Several of these genera are well-known phosphate solubilizers and plant growth promoters.

3.4 Relationships between soil properties and bacterial communities

RDA revealed that rhizosphere pH, available P, and acid phosphatase activity together explained 58.3% of the total variation in bacterial community structure. Available P (P = 0.002) and pH (P = 0.004) were the most significant explanatory variables. *Pseudomonas*, *Burkholderia*, and *Bacillus* were positively correlated with available P and acid phosphatase activity, and negatively correlated with pH. In contrast, *Acidobacteria* and *Actinobacteria* were positively associated with higher pH and lower available P.

3.5 Co-occurrence network analysis

The co-occurrence network of the P-efficient rhizosphere comprised 286 nodes and 1,024 edges, with a higher average degree (7.16) and modularity (0.68) than that of ‘M9’ (198 nodes, 562 edges, average degree 5.68, modularity 0.54). The proportion of positive correlations was higher in *M. hupehensis* (72.4%) than in ‘M9’ (58.9%), indicating more cooperative interactions among bacteria in the P-efficient rhizosphere. Keystone taxa in the P-efficient network included *Pseudomonas*, *Burkholderia*, and *Rhizobium*, whereas ‘M9’ network hubs were mainly *Acidobacteria* and *Actinobacteria*.

4. Discussion

Our results demonstrate that apple rootstocks with contrasting P efficiency differ markedly in plant growth, P status, rhizosphere chemistry, and bacterial community structure. The P-efficient *M. hupehensis* produced more biomass and accumulated more P than the P-inefficient ‘M9’ under low-P conditions, consistent with previous reports on genotypic variation in P efficiency among apple rootstocks. The higher root-to-shoot ratio and greater acid phosphatase activity in *M. hupehensis* suggest that root morphological and physiological adaptations contribute to its superior P acquisition. Root-mediated acidification and phosphatase secretion can mobilize sparingly soluble P, thereby increasing the pool of available P in the rhizosphere, as reflected by the higher available P concentration in *M. hupehensis* rhizosphere soil.

The distinct rhizosphere bacterial communities recruited by the two rootstocks support our second hypothesis. The higher bacterial diversity in the P-efficient rhizosphere may be attributed to greater root exudation and more favorable microhabitat conditions. Root exudates, including organic acids, sugars, and amino acids, serve as carbon sources and signaling molecules that shape microbial assemblages. The lower rhizosphere pH and higher available P in *M. hupehensis* likely created a niche that favored copiotrophic *Proteobacteria*, particularly *Pseudomonas*, *Burkholderia*, and *Rhizobium*. These taxa are frequently reported as efficient phosphate solubilizers and plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria. *Pseudomonas* and *Burkholderia* can dissolve inorganic phosphate via organic acid production, while *Rhizobium* can enhance P uptake through organic acid secretion and phosphatase activity. *Bacillus* and *Streptomyces* are also known for their ability to mineralize organic P and produce siderophores and antibiotics that suppress pathogens. The enrichment of these beneficial taxa in the P-efficient rhizosphere may thus form a positive feedback loop, in which root-mediated P mobilization recruits P-solubilizing bacteria that further enhance P availability and plant P uptake.

In contrast, the P-inefficient ‘M9’ rhizosphere was dominated by *Acidobacteria* and *Actinobacteria*, which are typically oligotrophic and adapted to nutrient-limited conditions. The higher abundance of these phyla may reflect the lower available P and higher pH in the ‘M9’ rhizosphere.

title: Arsenic biogeochemical cycling in paddy soil-rice system: Interaction with various factors, amendments and mineral nutrients
text:
Arsenic (As) contamination in paddy soil–rice systems poses a serious threat to food safety and human health, particularly in South and Southeast Asia where rice is the staple crop. Paddy soils are uniquely characterized by alternating aerobic and anaerobic conditions, which drive complex biogeochemical transformations of As and control its mobility, speciation, and bioavailability. Under flooded conditions, reductive dissolution of iron and manganese (hydr)oxides releases adsorbed arsenate [As(V)], which is subsequently reduced to the more mobile and toxic arsenite [As(III)]. This process is further mediated by microbial communities, root exudates, and the formation of iron plaques on rice roots, all of which influence As uptake and translocation within the plant.

The biogeochemical cycling of As in paddy systems is not governed by a single factor but arises from intricate interactions among soil physicochemical properties, redox dynamics, microbial activity, and external inputs. Amendments such as organic matter, biochar, silicon, and sulfur-bearing compounds can either immobilize or mobilize As, depending on dosage, timing, and soil conditions. Similarly, mineral nutrients including phosphate, silicate, and sulfate compete with As for adsorption sites or alter its speciation, thereby modulating its accumulation in rice grains. Despite extensive research, a comprehensive understanding of how these multiple factors interact to regulate As cycling remains incomplete.

This review synthesizes current knowledge on As biogeochemical cycling in paddy soil–rice systems, with particular emphasis on the interplay between environmental factors, soil amendments, and mineral nutrients. We aim to elucidate the mechanisms controlling As dynamics and to identify knowledge gaps and management strategies for mitigating As accumulation in rice.

title: Nutritional Intervention for the Intestinal Development and Health of Weaned Pigs
text:
Results and Discussion

The nutritional intervention markedly improved intestinal architecture and barrier function in weaned pigs. At d 14 post-weaning, jejunal villus height was 412 ± 21 μm in the intervention group versus 328 ± 19 μm in controls (*P* < 0.01), while crypt depth decreased from 246 ± 14 μm to 198 ± 12 μm (*P* < 0.05), yielding a villus-to-crypt ratio of 2.08 versus 1.33. These morphological gains coincided with a 38% reduction in serum diamine oxidase activity (18.6 vs. 30.1 U/L; *P* < 0.01) and a 27% increase in jejunal occludin mRNA expression, indicating enhanced epithelial integrity.

Microbial and inflammatory parameters corroborated these findings. Ileal *Lactobacillus* counts increased by 1.4 log₁₀ CFU/g (8.2 vs. 6.8; *P* < 0.01), whereas *Escherichia coli* declined by 0.9 log₁₀ CFU/g (*P* < 0.05). Fecal short-chain fatty acid concentrations rose from 58.3 to 79.6 mmol/kg wet weight (*P* < 0.01), with butyrate showing the largest relative increase (+52%). Serum interleukin-6 and tumor necrosis factor-α fell by 31% and 24%, respectively (*P* < 0.05), and secretory IgA in jejunal digesta increased by 45% (*P* < 0.01). Growth performance reflected these physiological benefits: average daily gain over 28 d was 386 ± 15 g versus 331 ± 17 g in controls (*P* < 0.01), and the diarrhea incidence dropped from 22.4% to 9.7% (*P* < 0.05).

The improvements are likely attributable to the synergistic actions of the intervention's components: glutamine and arginine supplying enterocyte fuel, and oligosaccharides selectively promoting beneficial taxa. Notably, the strongest correlations occurred between butyrate concentration and villus height (*r* = 0.71; *P* < 0.001), supporting a mechanistic link between microbial fermentation and epithelial repair. A limitation is the single 28-d time point; longer studies are needed to confirm persistence of these effects post-intervention. Overall, the results demonstrate that this nutritional strategy effectively mitigates post-weaning intestinal dysfunction and merits evaluation under commercial production conditions.

title: Genome-wide mapping of adult plant stripe rust resistance in wheat cultivar Toni
text:
Genome-wide mapping of adult plant stripe rust resistance in wheat cultivar Toni

Abstract

Stripe rust, caused by *Puccinia striiformis* f. sp. *tritici* (*Pst*), is one of the most destructive diseases of wheat worldwide. The deployment of adult plant resistance (APR) genes is a sustainable strategy for disease control. Wheat cultivar Toni has shown stable APR to stripe rust across multiple environments, but the underlying genetic basis remains unclear. In this study, a recombinant inbred line (RIL) population derived from a cross between Toni and the susceptible cultivar Avocet was evaluated for stripe rust severity across three field environments. A high-density single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) array was used to construct a genetic linkage map, and quantitative trait locus (QTL) mapping was performed. Three stable QTLs were identified on chromosomes 1BL, 4DL, and 7AS, designated *QYr.ton-1BL*, *QYr.ton-4DL*, and *QYr.ton-7AS*, respectively. *QYr.ton-1BL* explained 12.4–18.7% of the phenotypic variation, *QYr.ton-4DL* explained 9.8–14.2%, and *QYr.ton-7AS* explained 7.5–11.3%. All resistance alleles were contributed by Toni. The QTL on 4DL was mapped to a 2.1 cM interval flanked by markers *AX-94562134* and *AX-94562890*, while *QYr.ton-7AS* co-located with the known APR gene *Yr18* region. Haplotype analysis revealed that *QYr.ton-4DL* represents a potentially novel APR locus. These findings provide valuable genetic resources for marker-assisted selection and pyramiding of stripe rust resistance in wheat breeding programs.

Keywords: wheat; stripe rust; adult plant resistance; QTL mapping; *Puccinia striiformis*; Toni

1. Introduction

Wheat (*Triticum aestivum* L.) is a staple crop feeding more than one-third of the global population. Stripe rust, caused by *Puccinia striiformis* f. sp. *tritici*, poses a severe threat to wheat production, with yield losses reaching 40–60% under favorable epidemic conditions. The disease is particularly devastating in cool and moist regions, including the highlands of East Africa, the Middle East, and the western United States. Although fungicides can mitigate losses, their cost and environmental impact necessitate genetic resistance as the primary control strategy.

Two major types of resistance are recognized in wheat: seedling (all-stage) resistance and adult plant resistance (APR). Seedling resistance is typically race-specific, governed by major genes, and is often rapidly overcome by pathogen evolution. In contrast, APR is usually non-race-specific, quantitative, and more durable, making it a preferred target for breeding. Numerous APR genes have been characterized, including *Yr18*/*Lr34*, *Yr29*/*Lr46*, *Yr30*/*Sr2*, *Yr36*, and *Yr46*/*Lr67*. However, the genetic diversity of APR sources remains limited, and new resistance loci are urgently needed.

Wheat cultivar Toni, developed in the early 2000s, has exhibited consistent adult plant resistance to stripe rust across multiple locations and years. Preliminary inheritance studies suggested that Toni carries multiple APR genes, but their genomic locations have not been resolved. The objectives of this study were to (i) map quantitative trait loci (QTLs) for APR to stripe rust in a Toni × Avocet RIL population, (ii) evaluate the stability of QTLs across environments, and (iii) assess the potential novelty of the identified loci.

2. Materials and Methods

2.1 Plant materials

A population of 180 F₇ recombinant inbred lines (RILs) was developed from a cross between wheat cultivar Toni (resistant parent) and Avocet (susceptible parent) using single-seed descent. The parents and RILs were evaluated in field trials.

2.2 Field trials and disease assessment

Field experiments were conducted at three locations over two growing seasons (2021–2022 and 2022–2023): Yangling (Shaanxi, China), Tianshui (Gansu, China), and Lhasa (Tibet, China). Each trial used a randomized complete block design with two replications. Stripe rust epidemics were initiated by inoculating spreader rows with a mixture of prevalent *Pst* races. Disease severity was recorded three times at approximately 10-day intervals after flowering using the modified Cobb scale (0–100%). The area under the disease progress curve (AUDPC) was calculated for each line.

2.3 Genotyping and linkage map construction

Genomic DNA was extracted from leaf tissue of each RIL and the parents. All lines were genotyped using the Wheat 660K SNP array. After filtering for call rate (>95%), minor allele frequency (>0.3), and parental polymorphism, 3,842 high-quality SNP markers were retained. A genetic linkage map was constructed using JoinMap 4.1 with a logarithm of odds (LOD) threshold of 3.0. Markers were assigned to linkage groups based on the Chinese Spring reference genome (IWGSC RefSeq v2.1).

2.4 QTL analysis

QTL mapping was performed using composite interval mapping (CIM) implemented in WinQTLCart 2.5. For each environment, the AUDPC was used as the phenotypic trait. Permutation tests (1,000 iterations) determined the threshold LOD score for declaring a significant QTL. A QTL was considered stable if detected in at least two environments with a LOD score >3.0. The proportion of phenotypic variation explained (PVE) by each QTL was estimated from the final model. Epistatic interactions were tested using a two-way ANOVA for all pairwise marker combinations.

2.5 Haplotype analysis

To assess the novelty of the identified QTL, haplotype analysis was conducted using published resequencing data from 120 diverse wheat accessions. The physical intervals of the target QTL were compared with known APR gene regions.

3. Results and Analysis

3.1 Phenotypic variation

Stripe rust severity varied significantly among environments. The resistant parent Toni exhibited mean AUDPC values of 85.3, 102.7, and 78.9 across the three locations, whereas Avocet showed values of 612.4, 689.1, and 578.6, respectively. The RIL population displayed continuous and approximately normal distributions for AUDPC in all environments, indicating polygenic inheritance. Transgressive segregants were observed in both directions, with some lines more resistant than Toni and others more susceptible than Avocet.

3.2 QTL identification

Three stable QTLs were detected on chromosomes 1BL, 4DL, and 7AS, designated *QYr.ton-1BL*, *QYr.ton-4DL*, and *QYr.ton-7AS*. *QYr.ton-1BL* was identified in all three environments, with LOD scores ranging from 4.2 to 6.8, explaining 12.4–18.7% of the phenotypic variation. The resistance allele was contributed by Toni. *QYr.ton-4DL* was detected in two environments, with LOD scores of 3.9 and 5.4, explaining 9.8% and 14.2% of the variation, respectively. This QTL was mapped to a 2.1 cM interval flanked by SNP markers *AX-94562134* and *AX-94562890*, corresponding to a 4.8 Mb physical region on chromosome 4DL. *QYr.ton-7AS* was detected in all three environments but with lower effects, explaining 7.5–11.3% of the variation. Its confidence interval overlapped with the genomic region of *Yr18*, suggesting it may correspond to this known APR gene.

3.3 Epistatic interactions

Two significant epistatic interactions were detected. The interaction between *QYr.ton-1BL* and *QYr.ton-4DL* explained an additional 6.2% of the phenotypic variation, while the interaction between *QYr.ton-4DL* and *QYr.ton-7AS* explained 4.1%. Lines carrying all three resistance alleles exhibited the lowest mean AUDPC (72.4), while those carrying none had the highest (587.3), demonstrating additive effects.

3.4 Haplotype analysis

Haplotype analysis of the 4DL QTL region revealed that the resistance haplotype in Toni was distinct from those in wheat lines carrying *Yr18*, *Yr29*, *Yr30*, *Yr36*, or *Yr46*. Among 120 diverse accessions, only 8 (6.7%) shared the Toni haplotype, suggesting that *QYr.ton-4DL* represents a novel APR locus. In contrast, the 7AS QTL haplotype was highly conserved with the *Yr18* region, supporting its identity as *Yr18* or a closely linked gene.

4. Discussion

The identification of three stable APR QTLs in Toni provides new insights into the genetic architecture of stripe rust resistance in this cultivar. The major QTL on 1BL, explaining up to 18.7% of the variation, is particularly promising for breeding. Previous studies have reported APR QTLs on chromosome 1BL, including *Yr29* and *YrExp2*, but the marker interval of *QYr.ton-1BL* does not overlap with these genes, suggesting it may be a new locus. The 4DL QTL is especially noteworthy because it maps to a narrow interval and appears to be novel based on haplotype analysis. The 7AS QTL likely corresponds to *Yr18*, a well-characterized APR gene encoding an ABC transporter. The presence of *Yr18* in Toni is consistent with its pedigree, which includes the *Yr18*-carrying line Frontana.

The additive effects observed among the three QTLs underscore the value of pyramiding multiple APR genes. Lines combining all three resistance alleles exhibited significantly lower disease severity than those with one or two, suggesting that gene pyramiding can achieve near-immune levels of resistance under moderate epidemic conditions. The epistatic interactions detected further highlight the complexity of APR inheritance and the need for comprehensive QTL models in breeding.

The novelty of *QYr.ton-4DL* is supported by both its unique physical position and its rare haplotype among global wheat accessions. The 4.8 Mb interval contains several candidate genes, including a receptor-like kinase and a nucleotide-binding site–leucine-rich repeat (NBS-LRR) gene, which are plausible candidates for disease resistance. Fine mapping and functional validation of these genes are warranted.

The stability of QTLs across three diverse environments—representing the Yellow River basin and the Tibetan Plateau—suggests that these loci are effective under varying climatic conditions and *Pst* populations. This stability is a critical attribute for APR genes intended for broad deployment.

Several limitations of this study should be acknowledged. The population size (180 RILs) is moderate, which may limit the resolution of QTL mapping. Additionally, the use of a single bi-parental population restricts the detection of rare alleles. Future studies should employ larger populations, multi-parent advanced generation inter-cross (MAGIC) designs, and genome-wide association studies (GWAS) to validate and refine these QTLs.

5. Conclusion

This study identified three stable adult plant resistance QTLs for stripe rust in wheat cultivar Toni: *QYr.ton-1BL*, *QYr.ton-4DL*, and *QYr.ton-7AS*. The QTL on 4DL represents a potentially novel APR locus with a distinct haplotype. All resistance alleles were contributed by Toni and exhibited additive effects, with lines pyramiding all three QTLs showing the highest levels of resistance. These findings provide valuable genetic resources for marker-assisted selection and the development of durably resistant wheat cultivars.

title: Assessing the impact of digital financial inclusion on PM2.5 concentration: evidence from China
text:
Title: Assessing the Impact of Digital Financial Inclusion on PM2.5 Concentration: Evidence from China

Abstract
While the environmental consequences of financial development have been extensively studied, the ecological implications of digital financial inclusion (DFI) remain largely unexplored. This study investigates the impact of DFI on PM2.5 concentrations across 30 Chinese provinces from 2011 to 2021. Utilizing the Peking University Digital Financial Inclusion Index and a two-way fixed-effects model, we find that a 1% increase in DFI is associated with a 0.15% reduction in PM2.5 concentrations. Furthermore, mediation analysis suggests that this reduction is primarily driven by DFI facilitating industrial structural upgrading and promoting green technological innovation. The findings suggest that expanding digital financial services can serve as a dual-purpose strategy for promoting economic inclusivity and environmental sustainability.

Keywords: Digital Financial Inclusion; PM2.5; Air Pollution; China; Green Innovation; Sustainable Development.

---

 1. Introduction
China’s rapid industrialization has precipitated severe environmental challenges, with fine particulate matter (PM2.5) posing significant health risks to the population. Concurrently, the past decade has witnessed a financial revolution characterized by the rise of digital financial inclusion (DFI)—the provision of affordable financial services via digital channels to underserved populations. While DFI is lauded for poverty alleviation, its environmental externalities remain ambiguous. On one hand, digitalization reduces the physical footprint of banking; on the other, increased consumption facilitated by credit could theoretically increase emissions.

Existing literature often conflates general financial development with DFI, overlooking the unique role of digital platforms in allocating capital to green sectors. This paper addresses this gap by asking: Does DFI improve air quality in China? And if so, through what mechanisms? We hypothesize that DFI reduces PM2.5 by reducing the transaction costs for green technology financing and accelerating the shift from heavy industry to high-tech services.

 2. Materials and Methods

2.1 Data Sources
We constructed a balanced panel dataset covering 30 provinces in China (excluding Tibet, Hong Kong, Macao, and Taiwan) from 2011 to 2021.
- Dependent Variable: PM2.5 concentration (annual average, \(\mu g/m^3\)) was derived from satellite remote sensing data provided by the Atmospheric Composition Analysis Group.
- Independent Variable: The Digital Financial Inclusion Index (DFII), sourced from the Peking University Digital Financial Inclusion Research Center. This index covers coverage breadth, usage depth, and digitization level.
- Control Variables: To isolate the effect of DFI, we controlled for: GDP per capita (economic scale), secondary industry share (industrial structure), population density, foreign direct investment (FDI), and energy intensity.
- Mediating Variables: Green Technology Innovation (GTI) was measured by the number of green invention patents granted per 10,000 people. Industrial Structural Upgrading (ISU) was measured by the ratio of value-added of the tertiary sector to the secondary sector.

2.2 Model Specification
We employed a two-way fixed-effects model to control for time-invariant provincial characteristics and common time trends. The baseline econometric model is specified as:

\[
PM2.5_{it} = \alpha_0 + \alpha_1 DFII_{it} + \sum \beta_k Control_{kit} + \mu_i + \lambda_t + \epsilon_{it}
\]

Where \(i\) and \(t\) represent province and year, respectively. \(\mu_i\) denotes province fixed effects, \(\lambda_t\) denotes year fixed effects, and \(\epsilon_{it}\) is the error term. To explore mechanisms, we utilized a standard three-step mediation approach.

 3. Results

3.1 Baseline Regression
Table 1 presents the regression results. Column (1) shows the result without control variables, indicating a significant negative correlation. Column (2) introduces all control variables. The coefficient for DFII is -0.152 (p < 0.01), suggesting that a one-unit increase in the DFII index (on a scale of 0-300) predicts a 0.152 \(\mu g/m^3\) decrease in PM2.5. In terms of elasticity, a 10% increase in the DFI index corresponds to approximately a 1.5% reduction in PM2.5 concentrations.

*[Insert Table 1: Baseline Results - Invented Data]*
- *DFII: -0.152* (-3.42)*
- *GDP per capita: 0.211* (1.15)*
- *Industrial Share: 0.543 (2.21)*
- *R-squared: 0.682*

3.2 Mechanism Analysis
The mediation analysis reveals two distinct pathways. First, DFI significantly promotes industrial structural upgrading (\(\beta = 0.045, p < 0.05\)). By providing microloans and flexible credit to small-scale service enterprises, DFI accelerates the transition away from energy-intensive manufacturing. Second, DFI boosts green technology innovation (\(\beta = 0.012, p < 0.01\)). Digital platforms reduce information asymmetry, allowing investors to more easily identify and fund green startups.

3.3 Heterogeneity Analysis
We divided the sample into Eastern (developed) and Central/Western (developing) regions. The pollution-reduction effect of DFI is stronger in the Central/Western regions (-0.189) compared to the Eastern regions (-0.084). This suggests that DFI has a diminishing marginal utility; in regions where traditional finance is scarce, digital finance provides the critical capital needed to leapfrog to cleaner technologies.

 4. Discussion
Our findings contribute to the literature by identifying DFI as a novel determinant of environmental quality. The negative coefficient on DFII aligns with the "dematerialization" hypothesis, suggesting that digital finance allows economic growth to decouple from resource-intensive production.

The mechanism analysis supports the "structural dividend" theory. Unlike traditional bank lending, which often favors state-owned heavy industry, digital finance utilizes big data to assess credit risk, favoring light-asset, high-growth service and tech firms. By greasing the wheels of the service sector, DFI effectively reduces the regional reliance on coal-heavy manufacturing.

However, we must acknowledge limitations. The use of provincial data masks intra-provincial variations. Furthermore, while we controlled for FDI, the "pollution haven" hypothesis remains a potential confounder. Future research should utilize city-level data to capture localized spillover effects.

 5. Conclusion
This study provides empirical evidence that digital financial inclusion is a potent tool for environmental governance in China. By fostering industrial upgrading and green innovation, DFI significantly reduces PM2.5 concentrations. Policymakers should therefore view the expansion of digital financial infrastructure not merely as an economic inclusion strategy, but as a complementary environmental policy. To maximize these benefits, governments should incentivize digital financial platforms to prioritize lending to green technology sectors and small-to-medium enterprises in less developed regions.

title: Complexity perception classification method for tongue constitution recognition
text: Abstract: Tongue constitution recognition is a core diagnostic approach in traditional Chinese medicine, yet its subjective and experience-dependent nature limits objectivity and reproducibility. Existing computerized methods mainly focus on appearance features while overlooking the intrinsic complexity of tongue images, which arises from heterogeneous textures, irregular boundaries, and subtle constitutional variations. This paper proposes a complexity perception classification method for tongue constitution recognition. First, a multi-scale complexity perception module is constructed to characterize tongue images from complementary perspectives, including texture entropy, color distribution dispersion, and geometric irregularity. Second, a complexity-aware feature fusion strategy is developed to adaptively weight the extracted descriptors according to their discriminative contribution, thereby suppressing redundant information and enhancing constitutional cues. Finally, a complexity-guided classifier is designed to map the fused representations to corresponding constitution categories. Experiments are conducted on a self-built tongue image dataset covering multiple constitution types. The proposed method achieves superior performance compared with several state-of-the-art approaches in terms of accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score, demonstrating its effectiveness and robustness for automated tongue constitution recognition. The results suggest that complexity perception provides a promising direction for objective and interpretable tongue diagnosis in clinical practice.

title: Global commitments and China's endeavors to promote health and achieve sustainable development goals
text:
Global commitments and China's endeavors to promote health and achieve sustainable development goals

Abstract

The Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), adopted by the United Nations in 2015, place health at the center of global development, with SDG 3 specifically aiming to ensure healthy lives and promote well-being for all at all ages. However, progress toward global health targets has been uneven, and the COVID-19 pandemic has reversed decades of gains in many regions. This paper examines global commitments to health-related SDGs and analyzes China's endeavors to promote health and sustainable development between 2015 and 2022. Using a mixed-methods approach that combines quantitative analysis of synthetic health indicators with qualitative policy review, the study finds that China has made substantial progress in reducing maternal and child mortality, expanding universal health coverage, and improving infectious disease control. China's total health expenditure rose from 5.3% to 7.1% of GDP, while the under-five mortality rate declined from 10.7 to 6.8 per 1,000 live births. Nonetheless, challenges persist, including regional disparities, the growing burden of non-communicable diseases, and an aging population. The paper argues that China's domestic achievements and its increasing engagement in global health governance—through platforms such as the Belt and Road Initiative and South-South cooperation—offer valuable lessons for other developing countries. It concludes that sustained political commitment, strengthened primary health care, and inclusive international partnerships are essential to achieving the health-related SDGs by 2030.

Keywords: Sustainable Development Goals; global health; China; universal health coverage; health governance; South-South cooperation

1. Introduction

The 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, adopted by all United Nations Member States in 2015, established 17 interconnected goals to end poverty, protect the planet, and ensure prosperity for all. Health occupies a central position in this framework, not only as SDG 3 but also as a precondition and outcome of progress across other goals, including poverty reduction (SDG 1), quality education (SDG 4), and gender equality (SDG 5). The global community has repeatedly reaffirmed its commitment to universal health coverage (UHC), the strengthening of health systems, and the reduction of premature mortality from non-communicable diseases (NCDs).

Despite these commitments, global health progress has been uneven. Many low- and middle-income countries continue to face high maternal and child mortality, inadequate health financing, and shortages of qualified health workers. The COVID-19 pandemic further exposed the fragility of health systems worldwide, disrupted essential services, and pushed an estimated 100 million people into extreme poverty. In this context, the role of large emerging economies, particularly China, has attracted increasing attention.

China is home to approximately 18% of the world's population and has undergone rapid epidemiological and demographic transitions. Since 2015, the Chinese government has integrated the SDGs into its national development strategies, including the "Healthy China 2030" initiative, and has expanded its participation in global health governance. This paper therefore addresses two questions: (1) What progress has been made globally and in China toward health-related SDGs? (2) What policies and mechanisms have enabled China's achievements, and what challenges remain?

The paper is structured as follows. Section 2 describes the materials and methods. Section 3 presents results and analysis. Section 4 discusses the implications of the findings. Section 5 concludes with policy recommendations.

2. Materials and Methods

This study employs a mixed-methods design combining quantitative indicator analysis with qualitative policy review.

Quantitative data were drawn from a synthetic dataset constructed for illustrative purposes, modeled on the structure of the WHO Global Health Observatory, the World Bank World Development Indicators, and China's National Health Commission statistical yearbooks. Indicators included maternal mortality ratio (MMR), under-five mortality rate (U5MR), life expectancy at birth, total health expenditure as a percentage of GDP, out-of-pocket (OOP) health expenditure as a share of total health expenditure, and UHC service coverage index. The study period covers 2015 to 2022.
