Qualitative data comprised publicly available policy documents, including the "Healthy China 2030" Plan, China's National SDG Implementation Reports, and white papers on international development cooperation. These were analyzed using thematic content analysis to identify key policy instruments and implementation mechanisms.

Limitations should be noted. First, the quantitative data are simulated and intended only to illustrate analytical trends rather than to serve as official statistics. Second, cross-country comparisons are complicated by differences in data collection and reporting. Third, the qualitative analysis relies on publicly available documents, which may not capture informal or subnational policy processes.

3. Results and Analysis

3.1 Global progress and shortfalls

Between 2015 and 2022, global MMR declined from approximately 216 to 195 per 100,000 live births, and U5MR fell from 42 to 37 per 1,000 live births. Life expectancy at birth rose modestly from 72.3 to 73.1 years. However, these aggregate figures mask significant regional disparities. Sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia continue to account for the majority of maternal and child deaths. Moreover, the COVID-19 pandemic caused major disruptions: immunization coverage dropped for the first time in a decade, and tuberculosis and HIV service delivery declined in many countries. Financing gaps remain substantial; the WHO estimates that an additional US$ 10 billion per year is needed to strengthen health systems in low-income countries.

3.2 China's domestic achievements

China has recorded notable improvements across several health indicators. The MMR declined from 20.1 per 100,000 live births in 2015 to 15.7 in 2022, while U5MR fell from 10.7 to 6.8 per 1,000 live births. Life expectancy at birth increased from 76.3 to 78.2 years. Total health expenditure as a share of GDP rose from 5.3% to 7.1%, and the UHC service coverage index improved from 68 to 78. Out-of-pocket expenditure as a share of total health expenditure declined from 29.3% to 24.6%, indicating reduced financial hardship for households.

Key policy drivers include the expansion of basic medical insurance, which now covers more than 95% of the population; the strengthening of primary health care through community health centers and village clinics; and targeted programs for maternal and child health in rural and western regions. The "Healthy China 2030" initiative established quantified targets for NCD prevention, health literacy, and environmental health.

3.3 China's global health engagement

China has increasingly contributed to global health through South-South cooperation. Between 2015 and 2022, China dispatched medical teams to more than 50 countries, trained thousands of foreign health workers, and supported the construction of hospitals and malaria control centers, particularly in Africa. During the COVID-19 pandemic, China provided vaccines, protective equipment, and expert teams to over 100 countries. The Belt and Road Initiative has also incorporated health cooperation as a pillar, including the "Health Silk Road" concept.

Nevertheless, challenges remain. Regional disparities in health resources persist between eastern coastal provinces and western inland regions. NCDs now account for more than 80% of total deaths in China, driven by hypertension, diabetes, and cancer. Population aging—with over 14% of the population aged 65 and above—places additional pressure on long-term care and pension systems. Environmental pollution and mental health issues also require sustained attention.

4. Discussion

The findings suggest three broad lessons. First, sustained political commitment and institutional integration are critical. China's incorporation of SDG targets into national planning, coupled with fiscal investment and accountability mechanisms, has enabled measurable progress. Second, health system strengthening must prioritize primary health care and financial protection. China's experience shows that expanding insurance coverage and reducing OOP payments can improve access and equity. Third, domestic progress and global engagement are mutually reinforcing. China's participation in global health initiatives enhances its soft power while contributing to global public goods.

However, China's model is not directly transferable to all contexts. Its large fiscal capacity, strong central coordination, and rapid economic growth are not universally available. Moreover, questions remain about the sustainability of its health financing and the quality of care in remote areas.

For the global community, the analysis underscores the need for renewed multilateral commitment. The pandemic has demonstrated that health security is a collective responsibility. Achieving SDG 3 by 2030 will require increased financing, technology transfer, and equitable access to vaccines and medicines. China, as a major economy and a contributor to global health, can play a constructive role through transparent partnerships and alignment with international norms.

5. Conclusion

This paper has examined global commitments and China's endeavors to promote health and achieve the SDGs. While global progress has been uneven and the pandemic has created setbacks, China has achieved substantial domestic improvements in maternal and child health, UHC, and health financing. Its expanding engagement in global health governance offers both opportunities and responsibilities. To accelerate progress toward the health-related SDGs, this paper recommends: (1) strengthening primary health care and public health infrastructure; (2) reducing regional and urban-rural disparities through targeted resource allocation; (3) scaling up prevention and control of NCDs; and (4) deepening inclusive, rules-based international cooperation. Ultimately, health is both a marker and a driver of sustainable development, and collective action remains indispensable.

title: Effect of dietary isoleucine on the immunity, antioxidant status, tight junctions and microflora in the intestine of juvenile Jian carp (Cyprinus carpio var. Jian)
text: The intestine is not only the primary site for nutrient digestion and absorption in fish, but also a crucial immune and physical barrier against pathogens and harmful substances. An intact intestinal barrier depends on the coordinated function of tight junctions, antioxidant defense systems, and a balanced microbiota. Dietary amino acids have been increasingly recognized as key regulators of these intestinal functions beyond their classical roles in protein synthesis. Isoleucine (Ile), a branched-chain amino acid, is essential for fish and serves as a precursor for multiple metabolic pathways. Emerging evidence in mammals and some fish species indicates that Ile can modulate immune responses, enhance antioxidant capacity, and influence intestinal microbial communities. However, the effects of dietary Ile on the intestinal health of juvenile Jian carp (*Cyprinus carpio* var. Jian), an economically important freshwater species in China, remain largely unknown. Therefore, this study was conducted to investigate the effects of dietary isoleucine supplementation on the immunity, antioxidant status, tight junctions, and microflora in the intestine of juvenile Jian carp. The findings may provide a theoretical basis for optimizing isoleucine levels in aquafeeds to improve intestinal health and disease resistance in this species.

title: Study on the effect of digital economy on high-quality economic development in China
text:
Results and Discussion

Benchmark regression confirms that the digital economy significantly promotes high-quality economic development in China. The coefficient of the digital economy index is 0.237 (p < 0.01), indicating that a one-standard-deviation increase raises the high-quality development index by 0.184 standard deviations. After applying instrumental variable estimation to address endogeneity, the effect remains robust at 0.201 (p < 0.05). Heterogeneity analysis reveals that the impact is strongest in eastern regions (β = 0.312), moderate in central regions (β = 0.228), and weakest but still positive in western regions (β = 0.146), suggesting widening regional gaps. Mechanism tests show that technological innovation and industrial structure upgrading mediate 31.5% and 24.8% of the total effect, respectively. A threshold model identifies a critical digital economy level of 0.45, beyond which marginal returns increase substantially, implying network effects and economies of scale. Spatial Durbin results indicate a positive spillover effect (ρ = 0.183), meaning digital development in one province benefits neighboring provinces. These findings suggest that policymakers should accelerate digital infrastructure in central and western regions, foster innovation ecosystems, and promote cross-regional digital collaboration to narrow development gaps and sustain high-quality growth.

title: Tibetan women's perspectives and satisfaction with delivery care in a rural birth center
text:
Tibetan women's perspectives and satisfaction with delivery care in a rural birth center

Abstract

Background: In remote Tibetan regions, institutional delivery has increased, yet little is known about how women perceive and evaluate the care they receive in rural birth centers. Objective: This study examined Tibetan women's perspectives on and satisfaction with delivery care in a rural birth center in Qinghai Province. Methods: A cross-sectional survey using a structured questionnaire was conducted among 120 Tibetan women who gave birth in a rural birth center between January and June 2024. Data covered demographic characteristics, care experiences, and satisfaction across five domains: interpersonal care, information and communication, physical comfort, cleanliness and safety, and cultural respect. Results: Overall satisfaction was moderate (mean 3.82 ± 0.71 on a 5-point scale). The highest-scoring domain was cultural respect (4.21 ± 0.66), while information and communication scored lowest (3.34 ± 0.89). Women with a companion of choice and those who received explanations in Tibetan reported significantly higher satisfaction (p < 0.05). Conclusion: Tibetan women value culturally respectful care but are less satisfied with communication and informational support. Strengthening Tibetan-language communication and allowing birth companions may improve delivery care experiences in rural settings.

Keywords: Tibetan women; delivery care; birth center; patient satisfaction; cultural respect; rural health; maternal health

1. Introduction

Maternal health remains a global priority, and improving the quality of delivery care is essential for reducing maternal and neonatal morbidity and mortality. In China, institutional delivery rates have risen substantially in rural and minority regions over the past two decades. However, access alone does not guarantee quality. Women's experiences and satisfaction are increasingly recognized as key indicators of respectful maternity care and as factors influencing future health-seeking behavior.

Tibetan women in rural areas face distinct challenges, including geographic isolation, limited transportation, language barriers, and cultural practices surrounding childbirth. Many rural birth centers are staffed by Han Chinese or bilingual providers, while many Tibetan women, especially older or less-educated women, speak primarily Tibetan. Cultural differences in communication, modesty, and postpartum rituals may affect how care is received and evaluated. Despite growing attention to maternal health in Tibetan regions, few studies have specifically examined women's perspectives and satisfaction with delivery care in rural birth centers.

This study aimed to describe Tibetan women's perspectives on delivery care and to assess their satisfaction across multiple domains. A secondary aim was to identify factors associated with higher satisfaction, particularly language concordance and the presence of a birth companion. Findings are intended to inform culturally appropriate improvements in rural maternity services.

2. Materials and Methods

2.1 Study design and setting

A cross-sectional survey was conducted in a rural birth center in a Tibetan autonomous county in Qinghai Province, China. The center serves a predominantly Tibetan population and conducts approximately 300 deliveries annually. The study was approved by the institutional review board of the affiliated hospital, and written informed consent was obtained from all participants.

2.2 Participants

Women were eligible if they were Tibetan, aged 18 years or older, had given birth at the birth center between January and June 2024, and were able to provide consent. Women with severe medical or psychiatric conditions preventing participation were excluded. A total of 135 women were approached, and 120 completed the questionnaire (response rate 88.9%).

2.3 Data collection

Data were collected using a structured questionnaire administered face-to-face by trained bilingual research assistants within 48 hours after delivery. The questionnaire included sociodemographic items (age, education, parity, residence, antenatal visits), care experience items (language used by providers, presence of a companion, mode of delivery), and a 20-item satisfaction scale covering five domains: interpersonal care, information and communication, physical comfort, cleanliness and safety, and cultural respect. Each item was rated on a 5-point Likert scale (1 = very dissatisfied, 5 = very satisfied). The scale showed acceptable internal consistency (Cronbach's α = 0.86).

2.4 Data analysis

Data were analyzed using SPSS 26.0. Descriptive statistics summarized sociodemographic and satisfaction data. Independent-samples t-tests and one-way ANOVA were used to compare satisfaction scores by language concordance, companion presence, and parity. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05.

3. Results and Analysis

3.1 Participant characteristics

The mean age of participants was 28.6 ± 6.2 years. Most (68.3%) had completed primary school or less, and 72.5% lived in rural villages more than 30 km from the birth center. Nearly half (47.5%) were primiparous. Antenatal care attendance was high: 81.7% had at least four visits. Vaginal delivery accounted for 76.7% of births, and 23.3% underwent cesarean section.

3.2 Overall satisfaction

The overall mean satisfaction score was 3.82 ± 0.71. Domain scores were as follows: cultural respect 4.21 ± 0.66; cleanliness and safety 4.05 ± 0.72; interpersonal care 3.91 ± 0.78; physical comfort 3.62 ± 0.83; and information and communication 3.34 ± 0.89. The lowest-scoring individual items were "staff explained procedures in a language I understood" (3.12 ± 1.01) and "I was informed about my progress during labor" (3.21 ± 0.97).

3.3 Factors associated with satisfaction

Women who reported that providers sometimes or always spoke Tibetan during care had significantly higher overall satisfaction than those who received care only in Chinese (4.01 ± 0.65 vs. 3.52 ± 0.74, p = 0.003). Similarly, women who had a companion of choice present during labor reported higher satisfaction (4.03 ± 0.68 vs. 3.61 ± 0.73, p = 0.006). Primiparous women reported slightly lower satisfaction than multiparous women, but the difference was not statistically significant (3.74 ± 0.75 vs. 3.89 ± 0.69, p = 0.21). Mode of delivery was not significantly associated with satisfaction (p = 0.34).

3.4 Open-ended responses

In open-ended comments, women frequently praised staff kindness and the cleanliness of the facility. Common concerns included insufficient explanation of procedures, difficulty communicating with non-Tibetan-speaking staff, and limited privacy during examinations. Several women suggested that having a female Tibetan-speaking staff member available would improve their experience.

4. Discussion

This study provides insight into Tibetan women's perspectives on delivery care in a rural birth center. Overall satisfaction was moderate, with the highest scores in cultural respect and the lowest in information and communication. These findings align with broader evidence that respectful, culturally congruent care is highly valued by minority women, while communication barriers remain a persistent source of dissatisfaction.

The strong association between Tibetan-language communication and satisfaction underscores the importance of language concordance in maternity care. When women cannot fully understand explanations or express concerns, they may feel uninformed and anxious, even when clinical care is technically adequate. This is particularly relevant in rural Tibetan areas, where provider shortages make it difficult to ensure Tibetan-speaking staff at all times. Strategies such as training bilingual birth attendants, using trained interpreters, and providing Tibetan-language educational materials could help bridge this gap.

The finding that having a companion of choice was associated with higher satisfaction is consistent with global evidence on continuous labor support. In many Tibetan communities, family members, especially mothers or mothers-in-law, traditionally provide support during childbirth. However, some birth centers restrict companions for infection-control or privacy reasons. Reconsidering such policies in low-risk cases may improve women's experiences without compromising safety.

Cultural respect scored highest, suggesting that staff in this center made meaningful efforts to honor Tibetan customs, such as allowing traditional postpartum practices and respecting modesty. This is a notable strength. Nevertheless, the relatively lower scores in physical comfort and information provision indicate areas for improvement, including pain management, positioning options, and proactive communication.

This study has limitations. It was conducted in a single birth center, limiting generalizability. Satisfaction was measured shortly after delivery and may be influenced by relief or fatigue. Social desirability bias may also have inflated positive responses. Future research should include multiple sites, qualitative interviews, and follow-up assessments.

5. Conclusion

Tibetan women in this rural birth center reported moderate overall satisfaction with delivery care. They valued cultural respect but were less satisfied with communication and informational support. Language concordance and the presence of a birth companion were significantly associated with higher satisfaction. Improving Tibetan-language communication, enabling companion support, and strengthening patient-centered information exchange are practical steps that may enhance the quality of maternity care for Tibetan women in rural settings. Policymakers and health facility managers should prioritize culturally and linguistically appropriate care as essential components of maternal health quality.

title: Blended learning model via small private online course improves active learning and academic performance of embryology
text:
Blended learning model via small private online course improves active learning and academic performance of embryology

 Abstract

Background: Embryology is widely regarded as one of the most challenging preclinical subjects due to its dynamic three-dimensional developmental processes and dense terminology. Traditional lecture-based instruction often fails to sustain student engagement. This study evaluated whether a blended learning model delivered through a small private online course (SPOC) could improve active learning and academic performance in an undergraduate embryology course.

Methods: A quasi-experimental design was conducted with 186 second-year medical students assigned to either a blended SPOC group (n = 92) or a traditional lecture group (n = 94). The SPOC platform hosted micro-lectures, animated developmental sequences, virtual microscopy, and weekly online quizzes, while face-to-face sessions were reserved for case-based discussion and collaborative problem-solving. Outcomes included final examination scores, a validated active learning attitude scale, and course engagement metrics. Data were analyzed using independent-samples t-tests and analysis of covariance.

Results: The SPOC group achieved significantly higher final examination scores than the traditional group (82.4 ± 7.9 vs. 74.1 ± 9.3; p < 0.001; Cohen's d = 0.96). Active learning attitude scores were also higher in the SPOC group (4.21 ± 0.48 vs. 3.62 ± 0.55; p < 0.001). Online module completion averaged 88.6%, and 91.3% of SPOC students agreed that animated resources improved their understanding of developmental processes.

Conclusions: The SPOC-based blended learning model significantly enhanced both academic achievement and active learning attitudes in embryology, suggesting that strategically integrating online resources with interactive classroom activities can address the pedagogical challenges inherent to the discipline.

Keywords: blended learning; small private online course; embryology; active learning; medical education; academic performance

 Introduction

Embryology occupies a foundational position in medical curricula, underpinning subsequent study of anatomy, pathology, and clinical genetics. Nevertheless, it consistently ranks among the most difficult preclinical subjects. Students must simultaneously master temporal sequences, spatial transformations, and an extensive vocabulary of structures that appear, migrate, fuse, or regress within a compressed developmental timeline (Carlson, 2019). Conventional didactic lectures, which present static two-dimensional diagrams in linear sequence, are poorly suited to conveying these dynamic processes, and they frequently foster passive reception rather than active cognitive engagement.

Active learning—instructional approaches that require students to manipulate, apply, and reflect upon content rather than merely receive it—has repeatedly been shown to improve retention and transfer in science education (Freeman et al., 2014). However, simply adding active elements to a crowded lecture schedule is often impractical. Blended learning, which combines online delivery with face-to-face instruction, offers a potential solution by relocating content transmission to the online environment and reserving classroom time for higher-order activities.

Among blended models, the small private online course (SPOC) has gained attention in higher education. Unlike massive open online courses, a SPOC is restricted to a defined cohort, permitting instructors to align resources precisely with local learning objectives, monitor individual progress, and provide timely feedback (Fox, 2013). Despite growing enthusiasm, rigorous evaluations of SPOC-based blended learning in basic medical sciences remain limited, particularly in embryology, where visual and temporal reasoning demands are unusually high.

This study therefore aimed to determine whether a blended learning model delivered via SPOC improves (1) academic performance and (2) active learning attitudes among medical students studying embryology. We hypothesized that students in the SPOC-blended condition would outperform peers receiving traditional instruction on both outcome measures.

 Materials and Methods

 Study Design and Participants

A quasi-experimental, posttest-only design with a comparison group was employed during the spring semester at a university school of medicine. A total of 186 second-year medical students enrolled in the mandatory 16-week embryology course participated. Students were assigned to groups according to their existing laboratory sections to avoid timetable conflicts: 92 students formed the SPOC-blended group, and 94 formed the traditional lecture group. Baseline comparability was assessed using prior semester grade point averages (GPAs) and a pre-course knowledge test. The study protocol was approved by the institutional ethics committee, and informed consent was obtained from all participants.

 SPOC-Blended Group

The blended group received instruction through a structured SPOC hosted on a university learning management system. Each week, students completed three to five micro-lectures (6–10 minutes each) featuring narrated animations of developmental events such as gastrulation, neural tube closure, and cardiac looping. Additional resources included interactive three-dimensional models, virtual histology slides, and short formative quizzes with automated feedback. Online study was expected to require approximately 60–90 minutes per week.

Face-to-face sessions, held once weekly for 90 minutes, were redesigned around active learning. Sessions began with a brief clarification period based on quiz performance data, followed by case-based small-group discussions (e.g., diagnosing a ventricular septal defect from developmental principles), concept mapping exercises, and peer teaching. The instructor acted as facilitator rather than lecturer.

 Traditional Group

The traditional group received two weekly 45-minute didactic lectures covering identical content, supplemented by static PowerPoint diagrams and textbook readings. No online modules, quizzes, or structured pre-class preparation were provided. Laboratory sessions for both groups were identical and focused on specimen and model examination.

 Outcome Measures

Academic performance was measured by a 100-item final examination comprising multiple-choice and short-answer questions, with content validity established by three embryology faculty members. The examination included both recall and application items. Active learning attitudes were assessed using a 20-item validated Likert scale (1 = strongly disagree to 5 = strongly agree) covering engagement, self-regulation, and perceived value of interactive learning, administered in the final week. Internal consistency was acceptable (Cronbach's α = 0.87). Additional engagement metrics for the SPOC group included module completion rates and quiz participation.

 Statistical Analysis

Data were analyzed with SPSS version 26. Independent-samples t-tests compared group means for examination scores and attitude scales. Analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) controlled for prior GPA and pre-course test scores. Effect sizes were calculated using Cohen's d. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05.

 Results

 Baseline Characteristics

The two groups did not differ significantly in prior GPA (SPOC: 3.21 ± 0.42; traditional: 3.18 ± 0.45; p = 0.64) or pre-course knowledge test scores (SPOC: 41.2 ± 10.6; traditional: 40.5 ± 11.1; p = 0.66), supporting baseline comparability.

 Academic Performance

Students in the SPOC-blended group achieved significantly higher final examination scores than those in the traditional group (82.4 ± 7.9 vs. 74.1 ± 9.3; t(184) = 6.52, p < 0.001; Cohen's d = 0.96), representing a large effect. ANCOVA adjusting for prior GPA and pre-test scores confirmed the group effect (F(1, 182) = 38.7, p < 0.001, partial η² = 0.18). Subscore analysis showed that the advantage was most pronounced on application-oriented items (SPOC: 79.8%; traditional: 66.3%) compared with recall items (SPOC: 84.6%; traditional: 79.2%).

 Active Learning Attitudes

The SPOC group reported significantly higher active learning attitude scores (4.21 ± 0.48 vs. 3.62 ± 0.55; t(184) = 7.74, p < 0.001; d = 1.14). Item-level analysis revealed the largest differences in self-regulated learning ("I prepared before class and identified gaps in my understanding": 4.35 vs. 3.41) and perceived value of interaction ("Discussing clinical cases helped me apply embryology concepts": 4.42 vs. 3.58).

 Engagement Metrics

Average online module completion in the SPOC group was 88.6% (range 62–100%), and 84.8% of students completed at least 12 of 14 weekly quizzes. In a post-course survey, 91.3% agreed or strongly agreed that animated resources improved their understanding of developmental sequences, and 87.0% preferred the blended format over traditional lectures. Attendance at face-to-face sessions averaged 93.5% in the SPOC group versus 81.9% in the traditional group.

 Discussion

This study found that a SPOC-based blended learning model produced substantially better examination performance and stronger active learning attitudes than traditional lecturing in embryology. The large effect size on academic performance (d = 0.96) is consistent with meta-analytic evidence that blended instruction outperforms purely face-to-face delivery in health professions education (Liu et al., 2016), and it extends those findings to a subject with distinctive visuospatial demands.

Several mechanisms may explain the observed gains. First, animated and interactive online resources may reduce the cognitive load associated with mentally simulating dynamic developmental events, allowing students to allocate working memory to higher-order reasoning (Mayer, 2009). Second, the SPOC's weekly quizzes created a testing effect and provided instructors with diagnostic data to target classroom activities, a design consistent with flipped learning principles. Third, reserving class time for case-based discussion promoted elaboration and application, which likely accounts for the disproportionately large advantage on application-oriented examination items.

The attitude findings are equally important. Higher self-regulation scores suggest that the structured online component fostered habits of pre-class preparation and self-monitoring, while the preference for interactive sessions indicates that students recognized the value of the redesign. The higher attendance in the blended group further suggests that active classroom formats can counteract the attendance decline often seen in lecture-based courses.

 Limitations

Several limitations warrant caution. The quasi-experimental design cannot fully exclude selection effects, although baseline equivalence was demonstrated. The study was conducted at a single institution with one cohort, limiting generalizability. Outcome measures were confined to a single examination and self-reported attitudes; long-term retention and transfer to clinical clerkships were not assessed. Additionally, the additional time students invested in online modules may partly explain performance differences, and instructor enthusiasm could have introduced a novelty effect. Future multi-institutional randomized studies with delayed posttests are needed.

 Conclusion

A blended learning model delivered through a small private online course significantly improved academic performance and active learning attitudes in embryology compared with traditional lecturing. By relocating content transmission online and dedicating classroom time to interactive, case-based learning, the model addresses the specific pedagogical challenges of a visually and conceptually demanding discipline. These findings support the broader adoption of SPOC-based blended designs in preclinical medical education, provided that institutions invest in quality digital resources, faculty development, and robust evaluation systems to sustain and scale such innovations.

 References

Carlson, B. M. (2019). *Human Embryology and Developmental Biology* (6th ed.). Elsevier.

Fox, A. (2013). From MOOCs to SPOCs. *Communications of the ACM*, 56(12), 38–40.

Freeman, S., Eddy, S. L., McDonough, M., et al. (2014). Active learning increases student performance in science, engineering, and mathematics. *PNAS*, 111(23), 8410–8415.

Liu, Q., Peng, W., Zhang, F., et al. (2016). The effectiveness of blended learning in health professions: Systematic review and meta-analysis. *Journal of Medical Internet Research*, 18(1), e2.

Mayer, R. E. (2009). *Multimedia Learning* (2nd ed.). Cambridge University Press.

title: A pentavalent vaccine for rainbow trout in Danish aquaculture
text: Rainbow trout (*Oncorhynchus mykiss*) farming is a major component of Danish aquaculture, but production is constrained by several bacterial diseases that cause significant economic losses. This study evaluated the efficacy and safety of a novel pentavalent vaccine designed to protect rainbow trout against five major bacterial pathogens prevalent in Danish aquaculture: *Yersinia ruckeri*, *Aeromonas salmonicida* subsp. *salmonicida*, *Vibrio anguillarum*, *Flavobacterium psychrophilum*, and *Renibacterium salmoninarum*. The vaccine was formulated as a water-in-oil emulsion containing formalin-inactivated whole-cell bacterins and relevant antigenic fractions, and was administered by intraperitoneal injection to juvenile rainbow trout under controlled laboratory and field conditions. Fish were vaccinated at a mean weight of approximately 15–20 g and subsequently challenged with each pathogen via immersion or injection routes at defined intervals post-vaccination. Relative percent survival (RPS) was calculated for each challenge model. Vaccinated fish exhibited RPS values ranging from 72% to 94% depending on the pathogen, with the highest protection observed against *Y. ruckeri* and *A. salmonicida*, and the lowest against *F. psychrophilum*. Serum antibody titres measured by ELISA were significantly elevated in vaccinated groups compared with non-vaccinated controls for all five antigens, and remained detectable for at least 16 weeks post-vaccination. No significant adverse effects on growth performance, feed conversion ratio, or mortality were observed in vaccinated fish relative to controls during the 12-week safety monitoring period. Mild local inflammatory reactions at the injection site were transient and resolved within 4 weeks. These results demonstrate that the pentavalent vaccine confers robust and broad-spectrum protection against the five most economically important bacterial pathogens affecting rainbow trout in Danish aquaculture, and support its potential integration into routine vaccination programmes to improve fish health and reduce antibiotic use in the Danish trout industry.

title: Proteomic analysis in kidneys of Atlantic salmon infected with Aeromonas salmonicida by iTRAQ
text:
Proteomic analysis in kidneys of Atlantic salmon infected with Aeromonas salmonicida by iTRAQ

Abstract

Aeromonas salmonicida is the causative agent of furunculosis, a systemic disease responsible for substantial economic losses in Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar) aquaculture. The kidney is a primary target organ and a key immune site in teleosts, yet the molecular responses of salmon kidney to A. salmonicida infection remain incompletely characterized. In this study, we employed isobaric tags for relative and absolute quantitation (iTRAQ) coupled with liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) to profile the renal proteome of Atlantic salmon at 72 h post-infection with A. salmonicida. A total of 3,842 proteins were identified, of which 247 were differentially abundant (|log2 fold change| ≥ 1.2, p < 0.05), including 138 upregulated and 109 downregulated proteins. Functional enrichment analysis revealed that the differentially abundant proteins were predominantly associated with complement activation, acute-phase response, oxidative phosphorylation, lysosomal degradation, and cytoskeletal reorganization. Notably, complement component C3 and C9, serum amyloid A, and heat shock protein 70 were strongly upregulated, whereas proteins involved in mitochondrial energy metabolism and ion homeostasis were suppressed. These findings provide novel insights into the renal immune and metabolic reprogramming of Atlantic salmon during A. salmonicida infection and identify candidate biomarkers for disease monitoring and resistance breeding.

Keywords: Atlantic salmon; Aeromonas salmonicida; kidney; iTRAQ; proteomics; innate immunity; furunculosis

1. Introduction

Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar) is one of the most economically important aquaculture species worldwide. However, intensive farming practices have increased the incidence of bacterial diseases, among which furunculosis caused by Aeromonas salmonicida subsp. salmonicida remains a major threat despite the availability of vaccines. A. salmonicida is a Gram-negative, non-motile bacterium that produces a range of virulence factors, including the A-layer protein, extracellular proteases, and the type III secretion system, enabling it to evade host defenses and disseminate systemically.

The teleost kidney, particularly the head kidney, is a central immune organ that harbors hematopoietic tissues and acts as a principal site for immune cell differentiation and antibody production. It is also one of the first organs colonized by A. salmonicida during systemic infection. Therefore, characterizing the renal molecular response to infection is essential for understanding host-pathogen interactions and for developing effective intervention strategies.

Proteomics offers a direct readout of the functional state of cells and tissues. Among quantitative proteomic approaches, iTRAQ enables simultaneous comparison of multiple samples with high sensitivity and throughput, and has been successfully applied to study bacterial infection in various fish species. Nevertheless, proteomic data on the salmon kidney response to A. salmonicida are scarce. In the present study, we performed iTRAQ-based proteomic analysis of Atlantic salmon kidneys following experimental A. salmonicida infection, aiming to identify differentially abundant proteins and the biological pathways involved in the host response.

2. Materials and Methods

2.1 Fish and bacterial strain
Healthy Atlantic salmon (average weight 120 ± 15 g) were obtained from a commercial hatchery and acclimated in aerated freshwater tanks at 12 °C for two weeks. A virulent strain of A. salmonicida subsp. salmonicida (strain AS-01) was cultured in tryptic soy broth at 22 °C to mid-log phase, harvested, and resuspended in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) to a final concentration of 1 × 10^7 CFU/mL.

2.2 Infection experiment and sample collection
Fish were randomly divided into two groups (n = 30 per group). The infected group received an intraperitoneal injection of 100 μL bacterial suspension, while the control group received an equal volume of sterile PBS. At 72 h post-infection, fish were euthanized with MS-222, and kidney tissues were aseptically collected, snap-frozen in liquid nitrogen, and stored at −80 °C. Three biological replicates per group were used for proteomic analysis.

2.3 Protein extraction and iTRAQ labeling
Kidney tissues were homogenized in lysis buffer containing 8 M urea, 2 M thiourea, 4% CHAPS, and protease inhibitors. Proteins were precipitated with cold acetone, redissolved, and quantified using a Bradford assay. After reduction with dithiothreitol and alkylation with iodoacetamide, proteins were digested with trypsin at 37 °C overnight. Peptides were labeled with iTRAQ reagents (8-plex): control samples with tags 113, 114, and 115, and infected samples with tags 116, 117, and 118.

2.4 LC-MS/MS and data analysis
Labeled peptides were pooled, fractionated by strong cation exchange chromatography, and analyzed on a Q Exactive mass spectrometer coupled with an Easy-nLC 1000 system. Raw data were processed using Proteome Discoverer 2.2 against the Salmo salar reference database. Proteins with at least two unique peptides and a false discovery rate below 1% were retained. Differentially abundant proteins were defined as those with |log2 fold change| ≥ 1.2 and p < 0.05. Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analyses were performed using DAVID and clusterProfiler.

3. Results and Analysis

3.1 Overview of the renal proteome
A total of 3,842 proteins were confidently identified across all samples. Among them, 247 proteins showed significant abundance changes in the infected group relative to the control, comprising 138 upregulated and 109 downregulated proteins. Principal component analysis showed clear separation between infected and control groups, confirming the reproducibility of the biological replicates.

3.2 Functional enrichment of differentially abundant proteins
GO enrichment analysis indicated that upregulated proteins were mainly enriched in immune-related terms, including “complement activation,” “acute inflammatory response,” “antigen processing and presentation,” and “response to oxidative stress.” Downregulated proteins were enriched in “oxidative phosphorylation,” “ATP metabolic process,” “ion transport,” and “muscle contraction.”

KEGG pathway analysis revealed significant enrichment in the complement and coagulation cascades, lysosome, phagosome, and oxidative phosphorylation pathways. Notably, the complement pathway was the most significantly enriched, with multiple components showing increased abundance.

3.3 Key immune-related proteins
Complement component C3 and C9 were upregulated by 2.8-fold and 3.1-fold, respectively. Serum amyloid A (SAA), a major acute-phase protein, increased 4.2-fold. Heat shock protein 70 (HSP70) and HSP90 were elevated 2.5-fold and 2.1-fold. In addition, several lysosomal cathepsins (cathepsin B, D, and L) were upregulated, suggesting enhanced antigen degradation and presentation.

3.4 Metabolic and cytoskeletal alterations
Proteins involved in mitochondrial energy production, including NADH dehydrogenase, cytochrome c oxidase, and ATP synthase subunits, were downregulated by 1.5- to 2.3-fold. Conversely, cytoskeletal proteins such as β-actin and tubulin were moderately upregulated, possibly reflecting immune cell infiltration and tissue remodeling.

4. Discussion

The present study provides the first iTRAQ-based proteomic characterization of Atlantic salmon kidney during A. salmonicida infection. The pronounced upregulation of complement components C3 and C9 indicates robust activation of the complement system, which plays a critical role in opsonization and bacterial lysis. This is consistent with previous transcriptomic findings in other teleosts challenged with bacterial pathogens.

The strong induction of SAA and HSP70 reflects a systemic acute-phase response and cellular stress protection. SAA can modulate immune cell recruitment and cytokine production, while HSPs assist in protein folding and inhibit apoptosis, thereby supporting host cell survival during infection. The upregulation of lysosomal cathepsins suggests enhanced processing of bacterial antigens for MHC presentation, which is essential for adaptive immunity.

In contrast, the suppression of oxidative phosphorylation and ion transport proteins implies a metabolic shift in the infected kidney. This may be attributed to bacterial exploitation of host energy resources, mitochondrial dysfunction caused by virulence factors, or a trade-off prioritizing immune defense over energy-intensive processes. Similar metabolic reprogramming has been observed in mammalian sepsis models and in fish infected with other pathogens.

The cytoskeletal changes observed may reflect leukocyte infiltration and tissue repair processes. However, the precise cellular sources of these proteins remain to be determined, as whole-tissue proteomics cannot distinguish between resident renal cells and infiltrating immune cells. Future studies using single-cell or spatial proteomics could address this limitation.

Overall, the identified proteins and pathways provide a valuable resource for understanding the pathogenesis of furunculosis and for identifying potential biomarkers of disease progression or resistance.

5. Conclusion

In summary, iTRAQ-based proteomic analysis revealed that A. salmonicida infection induces profound changes in the Atlantic salmon kidney proteome, characterized by activation of complement and acute-phase responses, enhanced lysosomal function, and suppression of mitochondrial energy metabolism. These findings deepen our understanding of the renal host response to bacterial infection and offer candidate molecular targets for disease monitoring and selective breeding programs aimed at improving disease resistance in Atlantic salmon.

title: Elemental bioimaging of tissue level trace metal distributions in rice seeds (Oryza sativa L.) from a mining area in China
text:
Rice (Oryza sativa L.) is a staple food for more than half of the world's population, and its safety is of particular concern in regions affected by mining and smelting activities. Trace metals such as cadmium (Cd), lead (Pb), arsenic (As), and zinc (Zn) can accumulate in paddy soils and subsequently translocate into rice grains, posing potential health risks to consumers. Although bulk analysis of metal concentrations in rice grains has been widely reported, such measurements provide only average values and obscure the spatial distribution of metals within different seed tissues. This information is critical for understanding metal translocation pathways, storage sites, and potential toxicity mechanisms.

Elemental bioimaging techniques, including laser ablation-inductively coupled plasma-mass spectrometry (LA-ICP-MS) and synchrotron-based X-ray fluorescence (SR-XRF), have emerged as powerful tools for visualizing metal distributions in biological samples at the tissue and cellular levels. These methods offer high spatial resolution and multi-element detection capabilities, enabling the mapping of trace metals in rice seeds with minimal sample preparation. However, most previous bioimaging studies have focused on rice grown under controlled laboratory conditions or in soils with moderate contamination, and relatively few have examined seeds from actual mining-impacted areas where multiple metals co-occur at elevated concentrations.

In this study, we applied elemental bioimaging to investigate the tissue-level distribution of trace metals in rice seeds collected from a mining area in China. The specific objectives were to: (1) map the spatial distribution of Cd, Pb, As, Zn, and other elements in the embryo, endosperm, and aleurone layer of rice seeds; (2) compare metal accumulation patterns among different seed tissues; and (3) assess the implications of these distributions for food safety and human health. The results provide new insights into the translocation and storage of trace metals in rice grains under field conditions and contribute to the development of targeted mitigation strategies for metal-contaminated rice.

title: Rapid and real-time detection of black tea fermentation quality by using an inexpensive data fusion system
text:
Results and Discussion

The proposed data fusion system, integrating a low-cost colorimetric sensor array (CSA) and a miniature near-infrared (NIR) spectrometer, was evaluated for monitoring black tea fermentation. Fermentation samples were collected at 0, 2, 4, 6, and 8 h, and reference quality indices (theaflavins, thearubigins, and sensory score) were measured. Partial least squares (PLS) models based on CSA, NIR, and their fusion were constructed and compared (Table 1).

For theaflavins, the CSA-only model achieved a prediction R² (R²p) of 0.812 with a root mean square error of prediction (RMSEP) of 0.41 mg/g, while NIR-only gave R²p = 0.846 (RMSEP = 0.37 mg/g). The low-level fusion model improved performance to R²p = 0.918 (RMSEP = 0.26 mg/g), and the mid-level fusion model yielded the best result, with R²p = 0.943 and RMSEP = 0.22 mg/g, a 12.4% reduction in RMSEP relative to NIR alone. Similar trends were observed for thearubigins (fusion R²p = 0.927, RMSEP = 1.85 mg/g) and sensory score (fusion R²p = 0.936, RMSEP = 2.11 points).

These improvements are attributed to the complementary nature of the two sensors: the CSA captures volatile color-changing responses associated with polyphenol oxidation, whereas NIR reflects molecular overtone information of water, caffeine, and polyphenols. The mid-level fusion exploited latent correlations between the two data blocks, enhancing robustness against noise. Classification of fermentation degrees (light, moderate, over-fermented) using a fusion-based support vector machine achieved 96.7% accuracy, compared with 86.7% (CSA) and 90.0% (NIR). The total cost of the prototype was approximately US$180, and the detection time per sample was under 90 s, demonstrating its potential for rapid, on-site quality control in tea processing.

title: Improving Education About Breast Cancer for Medical Students in China
text:
Improving Education About Breast Cancer for Medical Students in China

Abstract

Breast cancer is the most common malignancy among women in China, yet evidence suggests that undergraduate medical education does not adequately prepare students for its clinical complexity. This study assesses current levels of breast cancer knowledge, clinical confidence, and educational satisfaction among Chinese medical students, and evaluates the effect of a structured supplementary teaching module. A quasi-experimental design was employed with 240 fifth-year medical students from three universities, divided into an intervention group (n = 120) receiving a 6-week blended module and a control group (n = 120) receiving standard curricula. Pre- and post-intervention assessments measured knowledge scores, diagnostic reasoning, and self-reported confidence. Results showed that the intervention group improved significantly in knowledge (from 62.4 to 84.7, p < 0.001) and confidence (from 2.8 to 4.2 on a 5-point scale, p < 0.001) compared with the control group. The findings indicate that targeted, integrated breast cancer education can meaningfully enhance student competence and should be embedded into Chinese medical curricula.

Keywords: breast cancer; medical education; China; clinical competence; blended learning; curriculum reform

1. Introduction

Breast cancer poses a substantial public health burden in China. According to recent epidemiological estimates, more than 400,000 new cases are diagnosed annually, and incidence continues to rise, particularly in urban populations (Zhang et al., 2022). Early detection, standardized treatment, and effective patient communication are critical to improving outcomes. However, these competencies depend heavily on the quality of medical education.

Despite the growing burden of breast cancer, undergraduate medical training in China remains fragmented. Breast cancer content is often distributed across surgery, oncology, radiology, and pathology courses, with limited vertical integration and insufficient clinical exposure. Many students graduate with theoretical familiarity but lack confidence in performing breast examinations, interpreting imaging, or discussing treatment options with patients (Li & Wang, 2021). Moreover, traditional lecture-based instruction dominates, leaving little room for case-based reasoning or multidisciplinary learning.

International studies have demonstrated that structured educational interventions—such as problem-based learning, simulation, and blended modules—can improve breast cancer knowledge and clinical skills (Harris et al., 2020). Yet few such initiatives have been rigorously evaluated in the Chinese context. This study addresses that gap by designing and assessing a supplementary breast cancer education module for Chinese medical students. The research questions are: (1) What are current levels of breast cancer knowledge and confidence among medical students? (2) Can a structured blended module improve these outcomes? (3) What are students’ perceptions of the module’s usefulness?

2. Materials and Methods

2.1 Study Design and Participants

A quasi-experimental pre-post design was used. Participants were 240 fifth-year medical students from three universities in eastern, central, and western China. Stratified random sampling was applied to ensure regional representation. Inclusion criteria were: enrollment in a clinical medicine program, completion of basic surgery and pathology courses, and voluntary consent. Students were assigned to the intervention group (n = 120) or control group (n = 120) based on their existing class groupings to avoid timetable conflicts.

2.2 Intervention

The intervention consisted of a 6-week blended learning module delivered alongside the standard curriculum. It included: (1) four online micro-lectures on breast cancer epidemiology, screening, pathology, and systemic therapy; (2) two face-to-face case-based seminars on diagnosis and multidisciplinary treatment planning; (3) a simulation session on clinical breast examination and patient communication; and (4) a reflective assignment on ethical and psychosocial aspects of breast cancer care. The control group received only the standard curriculum.

2.3 Instruments and Data Collection

A 40-item knowledge test was developed based on national guidelines and validated by five senior oncologists (Cronbach’s α = 0.87). A 10-item confidence scale (5-point Likert) measured self-efficacy in clinical tasks. A satisfaction questionnaire assessed perceptions of the module. Data were collected before and immediately after the intervention. Ethical approval was obtained from the institutional review boards of all participating universities.

2.4 Data Analysis

Quantitative data were analyzed using SPSS 26.0. Independent t-tests and paired t-tests compared group performance. Effect sizes were calculated using Cohen’s d. Qualitative comments were coded thematically.

3. Results and Analysis

3.1 Baseline Knowledge and Confidence

At baseline, the mean knowledge score was 61.8 (SD = 9.4) in the intervention group and 62.1 (SD = 9.1) in the control group, with no significant difference (p = 0.79). Baseline confidence was also similar (2.7 vs. 2.8, p = 0.62). Fewer than 40% of students correctly answered questions on sentinel lymph node biopsy or endocrine therapy indications, indicating specific knowledge gaps.

3.2 Post-Intervention Knowledge

The intervention group’s mean knowledge score rose to 84.7 (SD = 7.2), while the control group improved modestly to 66.3 (SD = 8.8). The between-group difference was significant (t = 17.42, p < 0.001, d = 1.52). Largest gains were observed in screening guidelines (+38%), pathological staging (+34%), and treatment sequencing (+31%).

3.3 Confidence and Clinical Reasoning

Confidence in performing clinical breast examination increased from 2.6 to 4.3 in the intervention group, compared with 2.7 to 3.0 in controls (p < 0.001). Similar patterns were found for interpreting mammography and explaining treatment options. In case-based reasoning, 78% of intervention students provided a correct multidisciplinary plan versus 46% of controls (χ² = 21.6, p < 0.001).

3.4 Student Perceptions

Satisfaction was high: 91% rated the module as “useful” or “very useful.” Thematic analysis identified three strengths: integration of theory and practice, exposure to real clinical cases, and improved communication skills. Suggested improvements included more simulation time and earlier introduction in the curriculum.

4. Discussion

This study demonstrates that a structured, blended breast cancer module can significantly improve knowledge, confidence, and clinical reasoning among Chinese medical students. The effect size for knowledge (d = 1.52) is substantial and comparable to findings from similar interventions in other settings (Harris et al., 2020). The results support the argument that breast cancer education should not remain an implicit byproduct of general surgery and oncology courses but should be explicitly designed and assessed.

Several factors may explain the intervention’s success. First, vertical integration helped students connect pathology, imaging, and treatment. Second, case-based seminars promoted active learning and multidisciplinary thinking. Third, simulation improved procedural confidence, a dimension often neglected in traditional Chinese medical education. These elements align with global calls for competency-based education.

However, challenges remain. Curricular crowding, limited faculty time, and uneven access to simulation equipment may hinder widespread adoption. The study also has limitations: it was quasi-experimental, relied on self-reported confidence, and followed students for only six weeks. Long-term retention and transfer to clinical practice were not measured.

Future research should examine longitudinal outcomes, include objective clinical assessments, and explore cost-effective models for resource-limited schools. Policy support is needed to mandate breast cancer competencies in national medical education standards.

5. Conclusion

Breast cancer education for Chinese medical students requires urgent strengthening. This study shows that a targeted blended module can produce meaningful gains in knowledge, confidence, and clinical reasoning. Integrating such modules into undergraduate curricula—supported by policy, faculty development, and simulation resources—would better prepare future physicians to address China’s rising breast cancer burden.

title: Photosynthesis research under climate change
text:
Photosynthesis research under climate change

 Abstract

Photosynthesis is the primary gateway for carbon entering the biosphere, and its response to rising atmospheric CO₂, warming, and altered water availability will largely determine the future strength of the terrestrial carbon sink. We synthesized a four-year (2021–2024) manipulative experiment on *Arabidopsis thaliana* and *Triticum aestivum* grown under factorial combinations of ambient/elevated CO₂ (420 vs. 720 µmol mol⁻¹), ambient/warmed temperature (+3.5 °C), and well-watered/drought conditions. Leaf-level gas exchange, chlorophyll fluorescence, Rubisco activity, and biomass accumulation were measured across vegetative and reproductive stages. Elevated CO₂ stimulated net photosynthetic rate (Aₙ) by 31.4% under well-watered conditions but only 12.7% under drought, indicating a strong negative interaction between CO₂ fertilization and water limitation. Warming reduced Aₙ by 8.9% on average, primarily through increased respiration and reduced Rubisco activation state, but the effect was partially offset under elevated CO₂. Drought was the single most damaging factor, reducing Aₙ by 42.3% and grain yield by 51.6%. Our results suggest that future photosynthesis research must move beyond single-factor CO₂ enrichment and prioritize multifactorial designs, dynamic acclimation, and crop-specific breeding targets to sustain productivity under compound climate stress.

Keywords: elevated CO₂; warming; drought; Rubisco; chlorophyll fluorescence; acclimation; carbon sink; multifactorial stress

 1. Introduction

Photosynthesis underpins nearly all terrestrial primary production and regulates the exchange of carbon and water between the land surface and the atmosphere. As atmospheric CO₂ concentrations continue to rise—surpassing 420 µmol mol⁻¹ in 2024—and global mean temperatures approach 1.3–1.5 °C above pre-industrial levels, understanding how photosynthetic machinery responds to concurrent environmental change has become one of the central questions in plant and climate science (IPCC, 2021).

Theoretically, elevated CO₂ should enhance carboxylation efficiency by increasing substrate availability for Rubisco and suppressing photorespiration. However, this "CO₂ fertilization effect" is frequently constrained by nutrient limitation, sink capacity, and down-regulation of photosynthetic capacity following prolonged exposure. Simultaneously, warming can accelerate enzymatic reactions up to an optimum but destabilizes thylakoid membranes and increases respiratory carbon losses beyond it. Drought closes stomata, limiting intercellular CO₂ and inducing oxidative stress. Critically, these factors do not act independently: elevated CO₂ often ameliorates drought stress by improving water-use efficiency, whereas warming can exacerbate drought through increased evaporative demand.

Despite decades of research, most photosynthesis studies still manipulate a single factor, producing results that are difficult to extrapolate to real-world, compound stress environments. This study addresses that gap through a four-year multifactorial experiment testing the hypothesis that (i) elevated CO₂ partially mitigates the negative effects of warming and drought on photosynthesis, and (ii) the magnitude of CO₂ mitigation declines as stress intensity increases.

 2. Materials and Methods

 2.1 Experimental design

The experiment was conducted from 2021 to 2024 in six walk-in climate-controlled growth chambers at the Institute of Plant Physiology, Aarhus University. We used a full factorial design with three factors: CO₂ concentration (ambient, 420 µmol mol⁻¹; elevated, 720 µmol mol⁻¹), temperature (ambient; warmed, +3.5 °C), and water regime (well-watered, 65% field capacity; drought, 30% field capacity), yielding eight treatment combinations replicated four times.

Two species were tested: *Arabidopsis thaliana* (Col-0 ecotype) and *Triticum aestivum* cv. Gladius. Plants were grown in 4-L pots filled with a 3:1 loam–sand mixture supplemented with slow-release fertilizer. Drought was imposed from the four-leaf stage onward by withholding water until target soil moisture was reached, maintained via gravimetric monitoring.

 2.2 Gas exchange and fluorescence measurements

Leaf gas exchange was measured using an open-path infrared gas analyzer system (LI-6800, LI-COR Biosciences) on the youngest fully expanded leaf. Measurements were taken at growth CO₂ and temperature, with a photosynthetic photon flux density (PPFD) of 1500 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹, leaf-to-air vapor pressure deficit of 1.2 ± 0.2 kPa, and 400 µmol s⁻¹ flow rate. Parameters recorded included net photosynthetic rate (Aₙ), stomatal conductance (gₛ), intercellular CO₂ concentration (Cᵢ), and transpiration rate (E). Light response curves (0–2000 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹) and A–Cᵢ curves (50–1200 µmol mol⁻¹ CO₂) were generated to estimate maximum carboxylation rate (Vcmax) and maximum electron transport rate (Jmax).

Chlorophyll fluorescence was measured with a pulse-amplitude-modulated fluorometer after 30 min dark adaptation. We recorded maximum quantum yield (Fv/Fm), effective quantum yield (ΦPSII), and non-photochemical quenching (NPQ).

 2.3 Biochemical assays

Rubisco activity was determined spectrophotometrically by coupling 3-phosphoglycerate formation to NADH oxidation. Rubisco activation state was calculated as the ratio of initial to total activity. Soluble protein and chlorophyll contents were quantified using standard Bradford and Arnon methods, respectively.

 2.4 Biomass and yield

At maturity, plants were harvested, separated into leaves, stems, and grains (wheat) or siliques (Arabidopsis), oven-dried at 70 °C for 72 h, and weighed. Grain yield components (spike number, grains per spike, thousand-grain weight) were recorded for wheat.

 2.5 Statistical analysis

Data were analyzed using three-way ANOVA in R (v4.3.1), with CO₂, temperature, and water regime as fixed factors and chamber as a random effect. Post-hoc comparisons used Tukey's HSD at α = 0.05. Results are presented as means ± standard error (n = 4).

 3. Results

 3.1 Leaf-level gas exchange

Elevated CO₂ significantly increased Aₙ across both species (p < 0.001). Under well-watered, ambient-temperature conditions, Aₙ rose from 18.2 ± 0.6 to 23.9 ± 0.8 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹ in wheat (+31.4%) and from 9.8 ± 0.4 to 12.7 ± 0.5 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹ in Arabidopsis (+29.6%). However, the CO₂ stimulation was strongly attenuated under drought, falling to +12.7% in wheat (p < 0.01 for CO₂ × water interaction).

Warming alone reduced Aₙ by 8.9% on average (p < 0.05), with the strongest decline in droughted, ambient-CO₂ plants (−15.2%). Under elevated CO₂, the warming penalty was reduced to −4.1%, confirming a significant CO₂ × temperature interaction (p < 0.05).

Drought was the dominant stress: Aₙ declined by 42.3% across all treatments (p < 0.001). Stomatal conductance followed a similar pattern, dropping from 0.38 ± 0.03 to 0.11 ± 0.02 mol m⁻² s⁻¹ under drought, while Cᵢ remained relatively stable, suggesting both stomatal and non-stomatal limitations.

 3.2 Photosynthetic capacity and Rubisco

Vcmax and Jmax were significantly reduced by growth under elevated CO₂ (−14.6% and −11.2%, respectively; p < 0.01), indicating downward acclimation. Warming further reduced Vcmax by 9.8% (p < 0.05). Rubisco activation state declined from 78.4 ± 2.1% in control plants to 61.3 ± 2.7% under combined warming and drought (p < 0.001), while total Rubisco content was less affected, implying regulatory rather than degradative down-regulation.

 3.3 Chlorophyll fluorescence

Fv/Fm remained above 0.78 in all well-watered treatments but fell to 0.69 ± 0.02 under combined warming and drought (p < 0.001). ΦPSII declined by 18.7% under drought, and NPQ increased by 34.2%, reflecting enhanced thermal dissipation. Elevated CO₂ partially restored ΦPSII under drought (+7.9%; p < 0.05).

 3.4 Biomass and yield

Total biomass increased by 24.8% under elevated CO₂ in well-watered wheat but only 8.3% under drought. Warming reduced grain yield by 13.4% at ambient CO₂ but only 5.2% at elevated CO₂. Drought reduced grain yield by 51.6% (p < 0.001), with thousand-grain weight the most affected component (−22.1%). Arabidopsis silique mass showed analogous trends.

 4. Discussion

Our results support the hypothesis that elevated CO₂ mitigates, but does not eliminate, the negative effects of warming and drought on photosynthesis. The 31.4% CO₂ stimulation observed under well-watered conditions is consistent with classic Free-Air CO₂ Enrichment (FACE) findings, but the sharp decline to 12.7% under drought demonstrates that water limitation constrains the benefit of additional carbon substrate. This likely reflects both stomatal closure limiting CO₂ diffusion and metabolic down-regulation associated with sink limitation.

The observed downward acclimation of Vcmax and Jmax under elevated CO₂ (−14.6% and −11.2%) is consistent with nitrogen dilution and reduced Rubisco synthesis when carbohydrate supply exceeds sink demand. Importantly, Rubisco activation state—not content—was most sensitive to combined warming and drought, suggesting that future breeding efforts should target Rubisco activase thermostability and redox regulation rather than simply increasing Rubisco quantity.

Warming's modest average effect (−8.9%) masks substantial treatment heterogeneity. Under drought, warming exacerbated stress through increased vapor pressure deficit and respiratory carbon loss, consistent with the "warmer drought" paradigm. The partial offset by elevated CO₂ (−4.1% vs. −15.2%) highlights the importance of multifactorial designs; single-factor warming experiments likely overestimate damage in a high-CO₂ future.

The fluorescence data indicate that photoprotection remained functional even under severe stress (Fv/Fm = 0.69), but increased NPQ suggests a substantial diversion of absorbed energy away from carbon fixation. This energy imbalance, combined with reduced Rubisco activation, explains the disproportionate yield loss (−51.6%) relative to leaf-level Aₙ decline (−42.3%).

Several limitations warrant mention. Growth-chamber conditions cannot fully replicate field microclimate, and our four-year window may not capture long-term soil nutrient feedbacks. Additionally, only two species were tested; extrapolation to C4 or perennial species requires caution.

 5. Conclusion

This study demonstrates that the future of photosynthesis research lies in multifactorial, ecologically realistic experimentation. Elevated CO₂ provides a consistent but stress-dependent benefit to photosynthetic rates and yield, while warming and drought interact synergistically to reduce carbon gain. The partial mitigation by elevated CO₂ diminishes as stress intensity increases, and Rubisco activation state emerges as a key regulatory bottleneck. We recommend that (i) future experiments adopt compound-stress designs, (ii) modeling efforts incorporate dynamic acclimation of Vcmax and Jmax, and (iii) breeding programs prioritize heat-stable Rubisco activase and improved water-use efficiency. Sustaining the terrestrial carbon sink under climate change will depend on how effectively these physiological insights are translated into crop improvement and ecosystem management.

title: The role of self-efficacy in mediating between professional identity and self-reported competence among nursing students in the internship period: A quantitative study
text:
Background: The internship period is a critical transitional phase for nursing students, during which professional identity and self-efficacy are considered important determinants of clinical competence. However, the mediating mechanism linking these constructs remains insufficiently explored.

Objectives: To examine the relationship between professional identity and self-reported competence among nursing students during their internship, and to test whether self-efficacy mediates this relationship.

Design: A cross-sectional, quantitative study.

Methods: A convenience sample of 428 nursing students undertaking clinical internships at three tertiary hospitals was recruited. Participants completed the Professional Identity Scale for Nursing Students, the General Self-Efficacy Scale, and the Competence Inventory for Nursing Students. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation analysis, and structural equation modelling with bootstrapping to examine mediation effects. All analyses were conducted with SPSS 26.0 and AMOS 24.0.

Results: Professional identity was positively correlated with self-efficacy (r = 0.52, p < 0.01) and self-reported competence (r = 0.58, p < 0.01), and self-efficacy was positively correlated with competence (r = 0.61, p < 0.01). Mediation analysis indicated that professional identity exerted a significant indirect effect on self-reported competence through self-efficacy (β = 0.21, 95% CI: 0.15–0.28), accounting for 36.2% of the total effect. The direct effect of professional identity on competence remained significant (β = 0.37, p < 0.001), suggesting partial mediation.

Conclusions: Self-efficacy partially mediates the relationship between professional identity and self-reported competence among nursing students during internship. Interventions aimed at strengthening professional identity and cultivating self-efficacy may enhance clinical competence. Longitudinal and multi-source designs are warranted to confirm causal pathways.

title: The burden of ambient air pollution on years of life lost in Wuxi, China, 2012-2015: A time-series study using a distributed lag non-linear model
text:
The burden of ambient air pollution on years of life lost in Wuxi, China, 2012–2015: A time-series study using a distributed lag non-linear model

Abstract

Ambient air pollution has been associated with increased mortality, but evidence on its impact on years of life lost (YLL)—a metric that weights deaths by remaining life expectancy—remains limited in medium-sized Chinese cities. This study aimed to quantify the burden of ambient air pollution on YLL in Wuxi, China, from 2012 to 2015. Daily data on YLL, air pollutants (PM₂.₅, PM₁₀, NO₂, SO₂, and O₃), and meteorological variables were collected. A distributed lag non-linear model (DLNM) combined with a quasi-Poisson regression was used to estimate the lag-specific and cumulative effects of each pollutant on YLL. Stratified analyses by age, sex, and season were performed. During the study period, a total of 187,432 YLL were recorded, with a daily average of 128.4 years. Each 10 μg/m³ increase in PM₂.₅, PM₁₀, NO₂, SO₂, and O₃ was associated with cumulative (lag 0–7) increases in daily YLL of 2.14 (95% CI: 1.32–2.96), 1.47 (95% CI: 0.89–2.05), 2.86 (95% CI: 1.74–3.98), 3.12 (95% CI: 1.85–4.39), and 1.05 (95% CI: 0.21–1.89) years, respectively. The effects were more pronounced in the elderly (≥65 years) and in the cold season. These findings indicate that ambient air pollution imposes a substantial burden on YLL in Wuxi, and targeted interventions are urgently needed.

Keywords: Ambient air pollution; Years of life lost; Distributed lag non-linear model; Time-series study; Wuxi; China

1. Introduction

Ambient air pollution is a leading environmental risk factor for global morbidity and mortality. The Global Burden of Disease Study estimated that outdoor particulate matter pollution contributed to 4.2 million premature deaths worldwide in 2015. China, as the world’s largest developing country, has experienced severe air pollution alongside rapid industrialization and urbanization. Numerous epidemiological studies in Chinese megacities such as Beijing, Shanghai, and Guangzhou have documented significant associations between air pollutants and daily mortality. However, most previous studies used mortality counts as the health endpoint, which treats deaths at different ages equally and may underestimate the burden of pollution on younger populations.

Years of life lost (YLL) is a complementary metric that accounts for the remaining life expectancy at the time of death, thereby reflecting premature mortality more accurately. YLL has been increasingly used in environmental epidemiology to assess the public health impact of air pollution. Nevertheless, studies on YLL attributable to air pollution in medium-sized Chinese cities are scarce. Wuxi, a city in the Yangtze River Delta with a population of approximately 6.5 million, has a typical subtropical monsoon climate and has experienced deteriorating air quality due to industrial and vehicular emissions. Understanding the pollution–YLL relationship in Wuxi is essential for local health policy.

The distributed lag non-linear model (DLNM) is a flexible statistical framework that can simultaneously capture non-linear exposure–response relationships and delayed effects over multiple days. In this study, we applied DLNM to a four-year time-series dataset to quantify the burden of five criteria air pollutants (PM₂.₅, PM₁₀, NO₂, SO₂, and O₃) on YLL in Wuxi from 2012 to 2015. We further examined effect modification by age, sex, and season.

2. Materials and Methods

2.1 Study area and data collection

Wuxi (31°34′N, 120°18′E) is located in southern Jiangsu Province, China. Daily data on deaths from non-accidental causes (ICD-10 codes A00–R99) were obtained from the Wuxi Center for Disease Control and Prevention for the period January 1, 2012 to December 31, 2015. For each death, age, sex, and date of death were recorded. YLL for each death was calculated as the remaining life expectancy based on the 2015 Chinese life table, stratified by age and sex. Daily YLL were then aggregated.

Daily mean concentrations of PM₂.₅, PM₁₀, NO₂, SO₂, and O₃ were retrieved from the Wuxi Environmental Monitoring Center. Meteorological data, including daily mean temperature and relative humidity, were provided by the Wuxi Meteorological Bureau. Missing pollutant values (less than 2% of the total) were imputed using linear interpolation.

2.2 Statistical analysis

A time-series quasi-Poisson regression combined with DLNM was employed. The core model was:

YLLₜ ~ quasi-Poisson(μₜ)
log(μₜ) = α + β·Xₜ,ₗ + ns(time, 7×4) + ns(Tempₜ, 3) + ns(RHₜ, 3) + γ·DOWₜ + δ·Holidayₜ

where YLLₜ is the daily years of life lost on day t; α is the intercept; Xₜ,ₗ is the cross-basis matrix for each pollutant generated by DLNM with a natural cubic spline for exposure (3 degrees of freedom) and a natural cubic spline for lag (4 degrees of freedom), with a maximum lag of 7 days; ns(time, 7×4) is a natural cubic spline with 4 degrees of freedom per year to control for long-term trend and seasonality; ns(Tempₜ, 3) and ns(RHₜ, 3) control for temperature and relative humidity; DOWₜ and Holidayₜ are indicator variables for day of week and public holidays. The pollutant effects were expressed as the change in daily YLL per 10 μg/m³ increase in concentration, with cumulative lag 0–7 effects reported.

Stratified analyses were conducted by age group (<65 and ≥65 years), sex (male and female), and season (cold: November–April; warm: May–October). Sensitivity analyses were performed by changing the degrees of freedom for time (3–5 per year) and the maximum lag (5–10 days). All analyses were conducted in R version 4.0.2 using the “dlnm” package. A two-sided p-value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.

3. Results and Analysis

3.1 Descriptive statistics

During the 1,461 study days, a total of 187,432 YLL were recorded, with a daily mean of 128.4 years (range: 32.1–312.7). The daily mean concentrations of PM₂.₅, PM₁₀, NO₂, SO₂, and O₃ were 58.3 μg/m³, 96.7 μg/m³, 42.1 μg/m³, 22.4 μg/m³, and 68.9 μg/m³, respectively. PM₂.₅ and PM₁₀ exceeded the Chinese National Ambient Air Quality Standard (GB 3095–2012) on 38.2% and 27.5% of days, respectively. Daily mean temperature was 16.8°C, and relative humidity was 72.3%. The daily YLL was highest in winter and lowest in summer, broadly mirroring the seasonal pattern of particulate matter.

3.2 Pollutant–YLL associations

After adjusting for confounders, all five pollutants were significantly associated with increased YLL. The cumulative lag 0–7 effects per 10 μg/m³ increase were as follows: PM₂.₅: 2.14 years (95% CI: 1.32–2.96); PM₁₀: 1.47 years (95% CI: 0.89–2.05); NO₂: 2.86 years (95% CI: 1.74–3.98); SO₂: 3.12 years (95% CI: 1.85–4.39); and O₃: 1.05 years (95% CI: 0.21–1.89). The exposure–response curves were approximately linear for NO₂ and SO₂, while PM₂.₅ and PM₁₀ showed steeper slopes at lower concentrations before plateauing. The lag structure indicated that most of the effect occurred within the first three days, with a small but significant delayed effect up to day 7 for particulate matter.

3.3 Stratified analyses

The effects of air pollution on YLL were consistently stronger in the elderly (≥65 years). For example, each 10 μg/m³ increase in PM₂.₅ was associated with 2.89 years (95% CI: 1.76–4.02) in the elderly versus 0.94 years (95% CI: 0.12–1.76) in those under 65. Males exhibited slightly higher estimates than females for PM₂.₅ and NO₂, although the differences were not statistically significant. Seasonally, the cold season showed larger effects for PM₂.₅, PM₁₀, and SO₂, whereas O₃ effects were more pronounced in the warm season. Sensitivity analyses confirmed that the results were robust to changes in model specifications.

4. Discussion

This study provides novel evidence that ambient air pollution is significantly associated with increased YLL in Wuxi, a medium-sized Chinese city. The cumulative effects we observed are comparable to or slightly larger than those reported in studies from Beijing and Shanghai. For instance, a 10 μg/m³ increase in PM₂.₅ was associated with 1.8 years of YLL in Shanghai, whereas our estimate was 2.14 years. The stronger effects in Wuxi may reflect differences in population susceptibility, air pollution composition, or healthcare access.

The biological mechanisms linking air pollution to premature death include oxidative stress, systemic inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, and autonomic imbalance. These pathways can exacerbate cardiovascular and respiratory diseases, leading to acute events and reduced life expectancy. Our finding that the elderly are more vulnerable is consistent with their higher prevalence of underlying chronic conditions and reduced physiological reserve.

The stronger effects in the cold season may be due to higher pollutant concentrations, lower ventilation, and increased respiratory infections. The significant O₃ effect in the warm season aligns with its photochemical formation under high temperatures and sunlight. The lag pattern suggests that acute exposure triggers immediate health events, while sustained exposure may contribute to delayed mortality.
